questions.q: Convert the number 142 in base 5 to base 10.
questions.e: Multiply each digit by 5 raised to its position power from right to left starting at 0. So, (1 x 25) + (4 x 5) + (2 x 1) = 25 + 20 + 2 = 47.
questions.p: Multiply every digit with 5 raise to power starting from zero for back. You go get (1 x 25) + (4 x 5) + (2 x 1), wey give you 25 + 20 + 2 = 47.

questions.q: Evaluate 34₆ + 15₆, leaving your answer in base 6.
questions.e: Add the digits column by column in base 6. 4 + 5 = 9, which is 1 group of 6 with 3 remainder; write 3 and carry 1. Then 3 + 1 + carry 1 = 5, giving 53₆.
questions.p: Add am column by column for base 6. 4 plus 5 na 9, e pass 6 with 3, so write 3 carry 1. Add 3 plus 1 plus 1, you go get 53 base 6.

questions.q: Evaluate 64₈ - 27₈, leaving your answer in base 8.
questions.e: Subtract column by column in base 8. In the units column, 4 - 7 is not possible, so borrow 1 (which is 8) to make it 12 - 7 = 5. In the tens column, 5 - 2 = 3, giving 35₈.
questions.p: Subtract for base 8. Borrow one 8 for back of 4 make e be 12, minus 7 na 5. Remaining 5 for front minus 2 na 3, so answer na 35 base 8.

questions.q: Express 73 in base 3.
questions.e: Successively divide 73 by 3, noting the remainders: 73/3 = 24 remainder 1; 24/3 = 8 remainder 0; 8/3 = 2 remainder 2; 2/3 = 0 remainder 2. Reading remainders upwards gives 2201₃.
questions.p: Divide 73 by 3 continuously and pack your remainder from bottom go top. You go get 2, 2, 0, 1, wey mean 2201 base 3.

questions.q: If 44_x = 34₈, find the base x.
questions.e: Convert 34₈ to base 10: (3 x 8) + 4 = 28. Then set 4x + 4 = 28. Solving gives 4x = 24, so x = 6.
questions.p: Change 34 base 8 to base 10, e go give you 28. Make 4x + 4 equal to 28. Solve am, 4x na 24, so x na 6.

questions.q: Convert 0.375 (base 10) to base 2.
questions.e: Multiply the decimal part successively by 2: 0.375 x 2 = 0.75 (carry 0); 0.75 x 2 = 1.5 (carry 1); 0.5 x 2 = 1.0 (carry 1). Reading downwards gives 0.011₂.
questions.p: Multiply the decimal part by 2 steady and pack the integer parts from top go bottom. You go get 0, 1, 1, so answer na 0.011 base 2.

questions.q: Evaluate (12₄)², leaving your answer in base 4.
questions.e: Convert 12₄ to base 10: (1 x 4) + 2 = 6. Square it: 6² = 36 in base 10. Convert 36 to base 4: 36/4 = 9 rem 0; 9/4 = 2 rem 1; 2/4 = 0 rem 2, giving 210₄.
questions.p: Change 12 base 4 to base 10, e give 6. Square am na 36. Now change 36 back to base 4, e go give you 210.

questions.q: What is the value of digit 5 in the number 2543₇ expressed in base 10?
questions.e: The digit 5 is in the second position from the left, representing 5 x 7². Since 7² = 49, 5 x 49 = 245.
questions.p: The 5 dey the second position from back, wey mean 5 times 7 raise to power 2. 7 power 2 na 49, times 5 na 245.

questions.q: Express 0.0004587 correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.e: Significant figures start from the first non-zero digit, which is 4. Counting three digits gives 4, 5, and 8, followed by 7. Since 7 is greater than 5, we round up the 8 to 9, giving 0.000459.
questions.p: Na from the first number wey no be zero you go start count, na 4. Make you count three numbers get 4, 5, 8, and then 7 dey back. Because 7 pass 5, you go add one join 8 make e turn 9.

questions.q: Chinedu bought a bag of rice for ₦24,000 and later sold it at a loss of 15%. What was the selling price?
questions.e: A 15% loss means Chinedu sold the bag at 100% - 15% = 85% of the original cost price. Calculate 85/100 × 24,000 = ₦20,400.
questions.p: If e loss 15%, e mean say e sell am for 85% of the original money. Just find 85 over 100 multiply by 24,000, na ₦20,400 you go get.

questions.q: Evaluate (0.03 × 0.004) / 0.06 leaving your answer in standard form.
questions.e: Multiply the numerators: 0.03 × 0.004 = 0.00012. Divide by 0.06: 0.00012 / 0.06 = 0.002. In standard form, 0.002 is written as 2.0 × 10⁻³.
questions.p: Multiply the top numbers first to get 0.00012, then divide am by 0.06 to get 0.002. When you write am for standard form, na 2.0 times 10 power minus 3.

questions.q: A basket contains oranges, mangoes, and pawpaws. 2/5 of the fruits are oranges, 1/3 of the remainder are mangoes, and the rest are 20 pawpaws. How many fruits are in the basket in total?
questions.e: Let total be T. Oranges = 2/5 T. Remainder = 3/5 T. Mangoes = 1/3 × 3/5 T = 1/5 T. Total of oranges and mangoes = 2/5 T + 1/5 T = 3/5 T. Pawpaws = T - 3/5 T = 2/5 T. Since 2/5 T = 20, T = 50.
questions.p: If oranges na 2/5, remaining na 3/5. Mangoes na 1/3 of remainder, wey be 1/5. Total of orange and mango na 3/5, meaning pawpaw wey remain na 2/5. If 2/5 represent 20 pawpaw, total fruit na 50.

questions.q: Round off 749,502 to the nearest thousand.
questions.e: To round to the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit, which is 5. Since it is 5 or more, round up the thousands digit (9) by 1, making it 750,000.
questions.p: To round to nearest thousand, check the hundreds number, na 5. Because na 5, you go add one join the thousand place, make everything turn 750,000.

questions.q: Evaluate 3²ˣ = 81, find the value of x.
questions.e: Rewrite 81 as a power of 3, which is 3⁴. Equating the exponents gives 2x = 4, so x = 2.
questions.p: Make you write 81 as 3 power 4. Since the base dey equal, na to equate the power 2x = 4, come divide by 2 to get x = 2.

questions.q: Simplify 2ⁿ⁺¹ × 4ⁿ⁻¹ / 8ⁿ completely.
questions.e: Express all terms with base 2: 4ⁿ⁻¹ = 2²ⁿ⁻² and 8ⁿ = 2³ⁿ. Combine numerator using laws of indices to get 2³ⁿ⁻¹, then divide by 2³ⁿ to get 2⁻¹ = 1/2.
questions.p: Change everything to base 2. Dem 4ⁿ⁻¹ go become 2²ⁿ⁻² and 8ⁿ go become 2³ⁿ. When you add up powers for top and minus bottom, you go remain with 2⁻¹ wey be 1/2.

questions.q: Solve for y in the equation 5ʸ⁻² = 1/125.
questions.e: Express 1/125 as 5⁻³. Equating the exponents yields y - 2 = -3, which means y = -1.
questions.p: Make you write 1/125 as 5 power minus 3. Make you match the powers together, so y - 2 = -3, and y go come equal to -1.

questions.e: Apply the negative sign to invert the fraction to (125/64)^(2/3). Find the cube root of 125/64 to get 5/4, then square it to get 25/16.
questions.p: That minus sign go first turn the fraction upside down to give (125/64)^(2/3). Take cube root of am to get 5/4, then multiply am by itself to get 25/16.

questions.q: If 9ˣ × 27^(1-x) = 3⁴, find the value of x.
questions.e: Express everything in base 3: 3²ˣ × 3^(3 - 3x) = 3⁴. This simplifies to 3^(3 - x) = 3⁴, so 3 - x = 4, which gives x = -1.
questions.p: Change all of them to base 3. You go get 3²ˣ times 3^(3 - 3x) equal to 3⁴, meaning 3 minus x equal to 4, so x na -1.

questions.q: Simplify √(81a⁸ × b⁴) completely.
questions.e: Take the square root of each factor: √81 = 9, √(a⁸) = a⁴, and √(b⁴) = b². Combining them gives 9 a⁴ b².
questions.p: Find square root of each number and letter inside. Square root of 81 na 9, a⁸ root na a⁴, and b⁴ root na b². Na so you get 9 a⁴ b².

questions.q: Find the value of k if 4ᵏ⁺¹ + 4ᵏ = 320.
questions.e: Factor out 4ᵏ: 4ᵏ × (4¹ + 1) = 320. This gives 4ᵏ × 5 = 320, so 4ᵏ = 64. Since 64 = 4³, k = 3.
questions.p: Factor out 4ᵏ from inside, you go get 4ᵏ times (4 + 1) = 320. Divide 320 by 5 to get 64, and since 4³ = 64, k must be 3.

questions.q: If 7ᵐ = 1/49, what is the value of m?
questions.e: Write 1/49 as 1/7², which is 7⁻². Comparing exponents with 7ᵐ yields m = -2.
questions.p: Make you write 1/49 as 7 power minus 2. Straight away, m go equal to minus 2.

questions.q: Simplify (27x³ y⁻⁶)^(1/3) / (8x⁻³ y³)^(-1/3).
questions.e: Cube root the first part to get 3 x y⁻². Apply the negative third power to the denominator to invert and simplify: it becomes (1/2) x y⁻¹. Division leaves 6 y⁻¹.
questions.p: Cube root the first bracket make you get 3 x y⁻². The second bracket wey get minus power go turn upside down, and when you divide am, x go cancel out make you remain with 6 y⁻¹.

questions.q: Find x if 2ˣ⁺² + 2ˣ⁺¹ = 24.
questions.e: Factor out 2ˣ⁺¹: 2ˣ⁺¹ × (2¹ + 1) = 24. This simplifies to 2ˣ⁺¹ × 3 = 24, so 2ˣ⁺¹ = 8. Since 8 = 2³, x + 1 = 3, giving x = 2.
questions.p: Factor out 2ˣ⁺¹ to get 2ˣ⁺¹ times (2 + 1) = 24. That gives 2ˣ⁺¹ times 3 = 24, so 2ˣ⁺¹ = 8, meaning x + 1 = 3 and x = 2.

questions.q: Evaluate log₃(27) + log₂(32).
questions.e: log₃(27) is 3 because 3³ = 27, and log₂(32) is 5 because 2⁵ = 32. Adding them together gives 3 + 5 = 8.
questions.p: log₃(27) na 3 because 3³ = 27, and log₂(32) na 5 because 2⁵ = 32. When you add dem together, you get 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.q: Solve for x if log₅(x) = 3.
questions.e: By converting the logarithmic equation to its exponential form, we get x = 5³. Therefore, x = 125.
questions.p: If you change am to index form, e go be x = 5³. When you calculate 5 times 5 times 5, you get 125.

questions.q: Simplify log₁₀(50) + log₁₀(2).
questions.e: Using the addition law of logarithms, log₁₀(50) + log₁₀(2) = log₁₀(50 × 2) = log₁₀(100). Since 100 is 10², the answer is 2.
questions.p: Make you use the plus law of log, wey mean say make you multiply 50 and 2. E go give you log₁₀(100), and since 10² na 100, your answer na 2.

questions.q: If log₂(x) - log₂(3) = 3, find the value of x.
questions.e: Using the subtraction law, log₂(x / 3) = 3. Converting to exponential form gives x / 3 = 2³ = 8, so x = 8 × 3 = 24.
questions.p: Subtract law talk say log₂(x / 3) = 3. If you carry am go index form, e mean say x / 3 = 8, so x = 8 times 3 wey be 24.

questions.q: Evaluate 3log_4(2) + 2log_4(8).
questions.e: Since log₄(2) = 1/2 and log₄(8) = 3/2, the expression becomes 3(1/2) + 2(3/2). This simplifies to 3/2 + 3 = 1.5 + 3 = 4.5.
questions.p: Make you find log₄(2) wey be 0.5 and log₄(8) wey be 1.5. Multiply dem by 3 and 2 respectively, you get 1.5 + 3, wey give you 4.5.

questions.q: Find x if 2log_3(x) = 4.
questions.e: Divide both sides by 2 to get log₃(x) = 2. Then, convert to exponential form: x = 3² = 9.
questions.p: Divide both sides by 2 first, e go remain log₃(x) = 2. Change am to index form, you go get x = 3², wey be 9.

questions.q: Given that log₁₀(2) = 0.3010 and log₁₀(3) = 0.4771, evaluate log₁₀(72).
questions.p: Break 72 down to 2³ times 3². Use log rule make you get 3 times log₁₀(2) plus 2 times log₁₀(3), wey be 0.9030 + 0.9542 = 1.8572.

questions.q: Solve the equation log_x(64) = 3.
questions.e: Rewriting the logarithmic equation in exponential form gives x³ = 64. Taking the cube root of both sides gives x = 4.
questions.p: Write am for index form, e go be x³ = 64. Find the cube root of 64, your answer na 4.

questions.q: If log₉(x) = 1.5, find the value of x.
questions.e: Write in exponential form: x = 9¹.5. Since 1.5 is 3/2, x = (9^(1/2))³ = 3³ = 27.
questions.p: Change am to index form: x = 9^(3/2). Find square root of 9 first, wey be 3, then cube am to get 27.

questions.q: Simplify completely: (log₂(8) + log₃(9)) / log₅(25).
questions.e: Numerator: log₂(8) = 3 and log₃(9) = 2, summing to 5. Denominator: log₅(25) = 2. Thus, 5 / 2 = 2.5.
questions.p: Upstairs na 3 + 2 wey give 5. Downstairs na 2. When you divide 5 by 2, you go get 2.5.

questions.q: Simplify the expression √75 - √27 + √12.
questions.e: Express each surd in its simplest form: √75 = 5sqrt(3), √27 = 3sqrt(3), and √12 = 2sqrt(3). Combine them: 5sqrt(3) - 3sqrt(3) + 2sqrt(3) = 4sqrt(3).
questions.p: Break down each surd to get 5sqrt(3), 3sqrt(3) and 2sqrt(3). When you add and subtract them, you go get 4sqrt(3).

questions.q: Evaluate (3sqrt(2) + 2sqrt(3))(3sqrt(2) - 2sqrt(3)).
questions.e: Use the difference of two squares formula (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b². Here, a = 3sqrt(2) and b = 2sqrt(3). So, (3sqrt(2))² - (2sqrt(3))² = 18 - 12 = 6.
questions.p: Na difference of two squares be dis. Just square the first one and subtract square of the second one, dat na 18 - 12 wey give 6.

questions.q: Rationalize the denominator of (4 / (√7 - √3)).
questions.e: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate, which is (√7 + √3). The denominator becomes (7 - 3) = 4, which cancels the numerator 4, leaving √7 + √3.
questions.p: Multiply top and down by the conjugate (√7 + √3). Downstairs go give you 7 - 3 = 4, wey go cancel the 4 for up.

questions.q: If p = 2 + √3, find the value of p² - 4p.
questions.p: Put p inside the expression or rearrange am as p(p - 4). When you substitute p, you get (2 + √3)(√3 - 2) wey give 3 - 4 = -1.

questions.q: Simplify √50 + √18 leaving your answer in the form ksqrt(2).
questions.e: Rewrite √50 as √(25 × 2) = 5sqrt(2). Rewrite √18 as √(9 × 2) = 3sqrt(2). Add them together: 5sqrt(2) + 3sqrt(2) = 8sqrt(2).
questions.p: Change √50 to 5sqrt(2) and √18 to 3sqrt(2). Add dem join make you get 8sqrt(2).

questions.q: Find the value of x if √(x + 5) - 2 = 1.
questions.e: Add 2 to both sides to get √(x + 5) = 3. Square both sides: x + 5 = 9. Therefore, x = 4.
questions.p: Carry -2 go other side make e become plus 2, e remain √(x + 5) = 3. Square both sides to get x + 5 = 9, so x = 4.

questions.q: Given that √x = 3sqrt(2) + √8, find the value of x.
questions.e: Simplify the right side: 3sqrt(2) + √8 = 3sqrt(2) + 2sqrt(2) = 5sqrt(2). Therefore, √x = 5sqrt(2) = √50. Squaring both sides gives x = 50.
questions.p: Simplify root 8 to 2sqrt(2). Add am join 3sqrt(2) to get 5sqrt(2). Square am back inside root to get root 50, so x = 50.

questions.q: Evaluate √48 / √3 without using tables.
questions.e: Combine under one root: √(48 / 3) = √16. The square root of 16 is 4.
questions.p: Put dem inside one big square root as 48 divide by 3, e go give you root 16. Root 16 na straight 4.

questions.q: If m = √5 and n = √2, find the exact value of (m + n)² + (m - n)².
questions.e: Expand both brackets: (m² + 2mn + n²) + (m² - 2mn + n²) = 2m² + 2n². Substitute m² = 5 and n² = 2 to get 2(5) + 2(2) = 10 + 4 = 14.
questions.p: When you expand both brackets, the middle terms cancel out to remain 2m² + 2n². Put m² = 5 and n² = 2, you go get 10 + 4 = 14.

questions.q: Let U be the universal set such that n(U) = 50. If set A and set B are subsets of U such that n(A) = 30, n(B) = 25, and n(A intersection B) = 10, find the number of elements in the complement of (A union B).
questions.e: First find n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B) = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. The complement of (A union B) is n(U) - n(A union B) = 50 - 45 = 5.
questions.p: Find union first: 30 plus 25 minus 10, wey be 45. To get di people wey dey outside A and B, minus 45 from di total 50, e come remain 5.

questions.q: If X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, Y = {3, 4, 5, 6, 7} and Z = {4, 5, 6, 7, 8}, find the set X intersection (Y union Z).
questions.e: First, find Y union Z = {3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. Then intersect this result with X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, which gives the common elements {3, 4, 5}.
questions.p: First join Y and Z together to get {3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. Then look for di numbers wey dey inside dat join-join set wey also dey inside X, na {3, 4, 5}.

questions.q: In a survey of 60 students in a hostel, 34 eat Rice, 28 eat Beans, and 12 eat neither food. How many students eat both Rice and Beans?
questions.e: Total eating at least one food = 60 - 12 = 48. Let x be those eating both. Using n(R U B) = n(R) + n(B) - x, we have 48 = 34 + 28 - x = 62 - x. Therefore, x = 62 - 48 = 14.
questions.p: Remove di 12 people wey no chop anything from 60, e remain 48 people wey dey chop either Rice or Beans. Add 34 and 28 to get 62, then minus 48 from 62 to get 14 people wey dey chop both.

questions.q: Given that n(U) = 100, n(P) = 55, n(Q) = 45, and n(P prime intersection Q prime) = 10, find n(P intersection Q).
questions.e: By De Morgan's laws, n(P prime intersection Q prime) = n((P union Q) prime) = 10. Thus, n(P union Q) = 100 - 10 = 90. Using n(P union Q) = n(P) + n(Q) - n(P intersection Q), we get 90 = 55 + 45 - x = 100 - x, which means x = 10.
questions.p: Di people wey no belong to P and Q at all na 10, meaning 90 people dey inside P union Q. Add P (55) and Q (45) to get 100, then minus di 90 total union from 100, you go get 10 for di middle.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the shaded region in a Venn diagram for the set operation (A intersection B prime) union (B intersection A prime)?
o: The symmetric difference of A and B
questions.e: The expression (A intersect B') represents elements in A only, and (B intersect A') represents elements in B only. Their union is the set of elements in either A or B but not in both, which is defined as the symmetric difference of A and B.
questions.p: Dis formula mean sey na only A side plus only B side wey shaded, wey be everything minus di middle intersection. Dat one na wet dem dey call symmetric difference.

questions.q: In a club of 50 members, 30 play Football, 24 play Basketball, and 6 play neither game. How many members play Football only?
questions.e: Total playing at least one game = 50 - 6 = 44. Let both be x. Then 30 + 24 - x = 44, so x = 10. Football only = n(F) - n(F intersection B) = 30 - 10 = 20.
questions.p: First find people wey dey play sports: 50 minus 6 = 44. Find those wey dey play both by doing (30 + 24) - 44 = 10. To get Football only, minus 10 from di total 30 people wey dey play Football, e remain 20.

questions.q: A trader bought a carton of frozen fish for ₦15,000 and sold it at a loss of 12%. Find the selling price of the carton of fish.
questions.e: The selling price is found by subtracting the loss percentage from 100% and multiplying by the cost price. That is, 88% of ₦15,000 gives ₦13,200.
questions.p: To find dis selling price, you just remove 12% loss from 100% to get 88%. Den multiply 88/100 by ₦15,000, and you go get ₦13,200.

questions.q: Calculate the simple interest on ₦45,000 for 4 years at 6.5% per annum.
questions.e: Simple interest is calculated using the formula (P × R × T) / 100. Substituting P = 45000, R = 6.5, and T = 4 gives (45000 × 6.5 × 4) / 100 = ₦11,700.
questions.p: Just use di simple interest formula, (P times R times T) divide by 100. Put 45,000 for P, 6.5 for R, and 4 for T, you go get ₦11,700.

questions.q: A man invested ₦80,000 in a cooperative society that pays compound interest at the rate of 5% per annum. Find the total amount at the end of 2 years.
questions.e: The total amount under compound interest is given by A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ. Substituting P = 80000, r = 5, and n = 2 gives 80000(1.05)² = ₦88,200.
questions.p: For compound interest, use A = P(1 + r/100) power n. Put 80000 for P, 5 for r, and 2 for n, you go get ₦88,200.

questions.q: If goods bought for ₦50,000 are sold at a profit of 20%, calculate the profit earned.
questions.e: Profit is calculated as 20% of the cost price. Therefore, (20 / 100) × ₦50,000 = ₦10,000.
questions.p: To find di profit, just calculate 20% of di ₦50,000 wey you take buy am. Dat one na 20 over 100 times 50,000, wey give you ₦10,000.

questions.q: A principal of ₦120,000 amounts to ₦150,000 in a certain period at simple interest. If the interest rate is 5% per annum, find the time in years.
questions.p: First find di interest by minus ₦120,000 from ₦150,000 to get ₦30,000. Den use T = 100I over PR to get 5 years.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks up his Ankara fabric by 40% above the cost price, but later offers a 10% discount on the marked price during a clearance sale. What is his overall percentage profit?
questions.e: Let cost price be 100. Marked price = 140. Discount of 10% on 140 is 14, so selling price = 140 - 14 = 126. Profit percentage = ((126 - 100) / 100) × 100 = 26%.
questions.p: Make cost price 100. Marked price go be 140. When you remove 10% discount from 140, selling price remain 126. Di profit percentage na 26%.

questions.q: Find the compound interest on ₦200,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually.
questions.e: Total amount A = 200000(1.10)² = ₦242,000. Compound Interest = Total Amount - Principal = 242000 - 200000 = ₦42,000.
questions.p: First find di total amount using 200,000 times 1.1 squared, wey be ₦242,000. Den minus di original ₦200,000 to get ₦42,000 interest.

questions.q: A man sold two radios for ₦24,000 each. On one he made a 20% profit and on the other he suffered a 20% loss. What was his overall net gain or loss?
questions.e: Cost price of first radio = 24000 / 1.20 = ₦20,000 (profit = ₦4,000). Cost price of second radio = 24000 / 0.80 = ₦30,000 (loss = ₦6,000). Total cost = ₦50,000, total selling price = ₦48,000, giving a net loss of ₦2,000.
questions.p: Find each radio cost price: first one na 24000/1.2 = ₦20,000, second one na 24000/0.8 = ₦30,000. Total cost na ₦50,000 but total selling price na ₦48,000, so e loss ₦2,000.

questions.q: If the simple interest on a certain sum of money for 3 years at 4% per annum is ₦6,000, find the principal amount.
questions.p: Use di formula for principal, P = 100I over RT. Put 6000 for interest, 4 for rate, and 3 for time, you go get ₦50,000.

questions.q: A phone was sold for ₦34,000 at a loss of 15%. At what price must it be sold to make a profit of 15%?
questions.e: Cost price = 34000 / 0.85 = ₦40,000. To make a 15% profit, the new selling price = 40000 × 1.15 = ₦46,000.
questions.p: First find di cost price by dividing ₦34,000 by 0.85, wey give ₦40,000. Den multiply ₦40,000 by 1.15 to get di new selling price of ₦46,000.

questions.q: If m varies directly as the square of n, and m = 18 when n = 3, find the value of m when n = 5.
questions.e: Since m varies directly as n², we have m = k × n². Substituting m = 18 and n = 3 gives 18 = k × 9, so k = 2. When n = 5, m = 2(5²) = 2 × 25 = 50.
questions.p: Since m dey vary direct as n², e mean say m = k × n². Put m = 18 and n = 3 inside, you go get 18 = k × 9, meaning k = 2. Now put n = 5, m go come be 2 × 25 = 50.

questions.q: Given that p varies inversely as q, and p = 4 when q = 7, find the value of q when p = 2.
questions.e: Inverse variation gives p × q = k. Thus, k = 4 × 7 = 28. When p = 2, 2q = 28, which gives q = 14.
questions.p: For inverse variation, p × q = k. So k = 4 × 7 = 28. If p = 2, na 2q = 28, con give us q = 14.

questions.q: Y is partly constant and partly varies directly as X. If Y = 11 when X = 2, and Y = 17 when X = 5, find the constant part.
questions.e: Let Y = A + bX. Using the given points: 11 = A + 2b and 17 = A + 5b. Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 3b = 6, so b = 2. Then A = 11 - 2(2) = 7.

questions.e: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, giving a right-angled triangle with legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Using Pythagoras theorem, the hypotenuse (radius) is √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 cm.
questions.p: Line from centre go divide chord into two equal parts, wey give 12 cm. Use Pythagoras theorem, radius na square root of (5² + 12²), wey be 13 cm.

questions.q: Points P, Q and R lie on the circumference of a circle with centre O such that angle PQR = 65 degrees. What is the size of the reflex angle POR subtended by the same arc at the centre?
questions.e: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc, so angle POR = 2 × 65 = 130 degrees. The reflex angle POR is 360 - 130 = 230 degrees.
questions.p: Angle for centre na two times angle for circumference, so angle POR na 130 degrees. To find reflex angle, minus am from 360 degrees, wey give 230 degrees.

questions.q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O. If angle APB = 70 degrees, calculate the size of angle OAB, where A and B are the points of contact.
questions.e: Triangle PAB is isosceles with PA = PB, so angle PAB = (180 - 70) / 2 = 55 degrees. The angle between radius OA and tangent PA is 90 degrees, so angle OAB = 90 - 55 = 35 degrees.
questions.p: Triangle PAB na isosceles, so angle PAB be 55 degrees. Angle between radius and tangent na 90 degrees, meaning angle OAB na 90 minus 55, wey be 35 degrees.

questions.q: Two parallel chords of length 16 cm and 12 cm are on opposite sides of the centre of a circle of radius 10 cm. What is the distance between the two chords in centimetres?
questions.e: Using half-chord lengths 8 cm and 6 cm with the 10 cm radius, the perpendicular distances from the centre are √(10² - 8²) = 6 cm and √(10² - 6²) = 8 cm. The total distance between the chords on opposite sides is 6 + 8 = 14 cm.
questions.p: Find distance from centre to each chord using Pythagoras, you go get 6 cm and 8 cm. Since dem dey opposite side of centre, add dem together to get 14 cm.

questions.q: An angle subtended at the circumference of a circle by an arc is 38 degrees. What is the angle subtended by the same arc at the centre?
questions.e: The angle at the centre of a circle is twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc. Therefore, the angle at the centre is 2 × 38 = 76 degrees.
questions.p: Angle for centre na two times angle for circumference. Just multiply 38 by 2, you go get 76 degrees.

questions.q: A chord of a circle of radius 17 cm is 30 cm long. Find the distance of the chord from the centre of the circle in centimetres.
questions.e: Half the chord is 15 cm. Using the radius of 17 cm as the hypotenuse, the distance from the centre is √(17² - 15²) = √(289 - 225) = √64 = 8 cm.
questions.p: Divide chord length by two to get 15 cm. Use radius 17 cm as hypotenuse, then calculate √(17² - 15²) to get 8 cm.

questions.q: The angle in a semi-circle is always equal to:
questions.e: By circle theorems, any angle subtended at the circumference by a diameter (which creates a semi-circle) is a right angle, measuring 90 degrees.
questions.p: Any angle wey diameter subtend for circumference na right angle, wey mean 90 degrees.

questions.q: Two intersecting chords AB and CD inside a circle intersect at point X. If AX = 4 cm, XB = 6 cm and CX = 3 cm, what is the length of XD in centimetres?
questions.e: By the intersecting chords theorem, AX × XB = CX × XD. Substituting the values gives 4 × 6 = 3XD, so 24 = 3XD, which means XD = 8 cm.
questions.p: Use chord theorem, multiply AX and XB, make am equal to CX times XD. 4 times 6 na 24, divide by 3 to get 8 cm for XD.

questions.q: A rectangular plot of land in Ikeja has a perimeter of 84 metres. If the length is 6 metres more than its breadth, calculate the area of the plot.
questions.e: Let breadth be x, so length is x + 6. Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 84, giving 2(2x + 6) = 84, so x = 18 m and length = 24 m. Area = 24 × 18 = 432 m².
questions.p: Make breadth be x, length na x + 6. Perimeter na 2(length + breadth) = 84, so x = 18 and length = 24. Area = 24 × 18 wey give 432 m².

questions.q: Find the total surface area of a solid cylinder whose base radius is 7 cm and height is 10 cm. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: Total surface area of a cylinder is 2pi × r × (r + h). Substituting r = 7 and h = 10 gives 2(22/7) × 7(7 + 10) = 44 × 17 = 748 cm².
questions.p: Total surface area formula na 2pi × r × (r + h). Put r = 7 and h = 10 inside, you go get 2(22/7) × 7 × 17 = 748 cm².

questions.q: A sector of a circle with radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Calculate the area of this sector. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: Area of a sector = (theta / 360) × π × r². Substituting theta = 60 and r = 14 gives (60 / 360) × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = (1/6) × 616 = 102.67 cm².
questions.p: Area of sector na (theta / 360) × π × r². Put theta = 60 and r = 14, e go give (1/6) × (22/7) × 196 = 102.67 cm².

questions.q: The volume of a right circular cone is 308 cm³. If its base radius is 7 cm, find its vertical height. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h. Thus 308 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 49h, which simplifies to 308 = (154/3) × h, giving h = (308 × 3) / 154 = 6 cm.
questions.p: Volume of cone formula na (1/3) × π × r² × h. Put 308 for volume and r = 7, you go get 308 = (154/3) × h, so h = 6 cm.

questions.q: Calculate the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 12 cm and 18 cm long, and the perpendicular distance between them is 8 cm.
questions.e: Area of a trapezium = 0.5(sum of parallel sides) × height. Area = 0.5(12 + 18) × 8 = 0.5 × 30 × 8 = 120 cm².
questions.p: Area of trapezium na half times sum of parallel sides times height. E go be 0.5(12 + 18) × 8 = 120 cm².

questions.q: The perimeter of a regular hexagon is 72 cm. Find the area of the hexagon.
questions.e: A regular hexagon has 6 sides, so side length s = 72 / 6 = 12 cm. The area is given by (3√3 / 2) × s² = (3√3 / 2) × 144 = 216√3 cm².
questions.p: Hexagon get 6 sides, so one side na 72 / 6 = 12 cm. Area formula for regular hexagon na (3√3 / 2) × s², wey give 216√3 cm².

questions.q: An open cylindrical drum has a height of 1.2 m and a base diameter of 70 cm. Calculate the outer curved surface area in square metres. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: Radius r = 70 cm / 2 = 35 cm = 0.35 m. Curved surface area of an open cylinder = 2pi × r × h. Thus 2(22/7) × 0.35 × 1.2 = 2.64 m².
questions.p: Radius na 0.35 m. Curved surface area formula for cylinder na 2pi × r × h. Multiply 2(22/7) × 0.35 × 1.2, you go get 2.64 m².

questions.q: What is the area of a triangle whose sides measure 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
questions.e: Use Heron's formula. Semi-perimeter s = (13 + 14 + 15) / 2 = 21 cm. Area = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056 = 84 cm².
questions.p: Use Heron formula since you know all three sides. Semi-perimeter s = 21. Area = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = 84 cm².

questions.q: A wheel has a diameter of 84 cm. How many complete revolutions will it make over a distance of 1.584 km? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: Circumference = π × d = (22/7) × 84 = 264 cm = 2.64 m. Total distance = 1.584 km = 1584 m. Number of revolutions = 1584 / 2.64 = 600.
questions.p: Find distance of one round (circumference), wey be (22/7) × 84 = 264 cm or 2.64 m. Divide total distance (1584 m) by 2.64 to get 600 revolutions.

questions.q: Find the distance between the points P(2, 3) and Q(5, 7) in a Cartesian plane.
questions.e: Use the distance formula d = √((x_2 - x_1)² + (y_2 - y_1)²). Substituting the coordinates gives √((5 - 2)² + (7 - 3)²) = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.
questions.p: Make you use di distance formula. Na √((5 - 2)² + (7 - 3)²) wey go give us √(9 + 16) = √25, wey be 5.

questions.q: Determine the midpoint of the line segment joining the points A(-1, 4) and B(5, -2).
questions.e: The midpoint formula is ((x_1 + x_2)/2, (y_1 + y_2)/2). Substituting the values gives ((-1 + 5)/2, (4 + -2)/2) = (4/2, 2/2) = (2, 1).
questions.p: To find midpoint, add di x-coordinates divide by 2, and add di y-coordinates divide by 2. E go give us (2, 1).

questions.q: Calculate the gradient of the straight line passing through the points R(2, -3) and S(6, 5).
questions.e: The gradient m is given by (y_2 - y_1)/(x_2 - x_1). Substituting the points yields (5 - (-3)) / (6 - 2) = 8 / 4 = 2.
questions.p: Gradient na change in y divide by change in x. Na (5 - (-3)) over (6 - 2), wey bi 8 over 4, and dat na 2.

questions.q: Find the equation of the straight line that has a gradient of 3 and passes through the point (1, 4).
questions.e: Using the point-slope form y - y_1 = m(x - x_1), we get y - 4 = 3(x - 1). Expanding this gives y - 4 = 3x - 3, which simplifies to y = 3x + 1.
questions.p: Use di formula y - y_1 = m(x - x_1). Put m = 3 and point (1, 4), e go give you y - 4 = 3(x - 1), wey come be y = 3x + 1.

questions.q: A line passes through the points (k, 2) and (3, 6) with a gradient of 2. Find the value of k.
questions.e: Set up the gradient formula: (6 - 2) / (3 - k) = 2. This simplifies to 4 / (3 - k) = 2, so 3 - k = 2, which gives k = 1.
questions.p: Make you write di gradient formula with di numbers: (6 - 2) / (3 - k) = 2. Cross multiply and solve for k, you go get 1.

questions.q: Find the y-intercept of the line whose equation is 3x - 4y = 12.
questions.e: To find the y-intercept, set x = 0 in the equation. We get 3(0) - 4y = 12, so -4y = 12, which gives y = -3.
questions.p: To get y-intercept, put x = 0 inside di equation. You go get -4y = 12, so y na -3.

questions.q: Find the equation of the line that is perpendicular to y = -2x + 5 and passes through the point (4, 1).
questions.e: The gradient of the given line is -2. A perpendicular line has a negative reciprocal gradient, so m_2 = 1/2. Using y - 1 = (1/2)(x - 4), we get y - 1 = (1/2)x - 2, which simplifies to y = (1/2)x - 1.
questions.p: Perpendicular gradient na negative reciprocal, so m = 1/2. Use point (4, 1) inside equation, you go get y = (1/2)x - 1.

questions.q: If the points (1, 2), (3, 8), and (5, k) are collinear, find the value of k.
questions.e: Collinear points have the same gradient between any pairs. Equating gradients from (1,2) to (3,8) and (3,8) to (5,k): (8 - 2)/(3 - 1) = (k - 8)/(5 - 3). This gives 6/2 = (k - 8)/2, so 3 = (k - 8)/2, leading to k - 8 = 6, and k = 14.
questions.p: Since dem dey same straight line, gradient between first two points must equal gradient between last two points. Solve am and you go get k = 14.

questions.q: Find the acute angle that the line y = √3x + 5 makes with the positive direction of the x-axis.
questions.e: The gradient of the line is m = √3. Since gradient is equal to tan(theta), we have tan(theta) = √3. Therefore, theta = arctan(√3) = 60 degrees.
questions.p: Gradient na tan of di angle. Since m = √3, tan(theta) = √3, meaning theta na 60 degrees.

questions.q: In a right-angled triangle PQR where angle Q is 90 degrees, if PQ = 3 cm and QR = 4 cm, what is the value of sin R?
questions.e: Using Pythagoras theorem, the hypotenuse PR is √(3² + 4²) = 5. Sine is defined as opposite/hypotenuse, so sin R = PQ/PR = 3/5.
questions.p: If we use Pythagoras, the long side PR na 5. Since sine na opposite over hypotenuse, we go get 3 divided by 5.

questions.q: If cos x = 1/2 and x is an acute angle, find the value of tan x.
questions.e: Since cos x = 1/2, x = 60 degrees. Tan 60 degrees is equal to √3.
questions.p: Because cos x na 1/2, e mean say x na 60 degrees. If you find tan of 60 degrees, you go get √3.

questions.q: A student stands 10 meters away from the base of a flagpole and observes the top at an angle of elevation of 45 degrees. How tall is the flagpole?
questions.e: In a triangle with 45 degrees, the opposite side equals the adjacent side. Since adjacent = 10m, the height is 10m.
questions.p: Because the angle na 45 degrees, the height must be the same as the distance from the base. So the height na 10 meters.

questions.q: Simplify (sin² theta + cos² theta) / (tan² theta + 1).
questions.e: The numerator sin² theta + cos² theta = 1. The denominator tan² theta + 1 = sec² theta. Thus, 1/sec² theta = cos² theta.
questions.p: Top side na 1, and bottom side na sec² theta. When you divide 1 by sec² theta, you go get cos² theta.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, side a = 7 cm, side b = 8 cm, and angle C = 60 degrees. Find the length of side c.
questions.e: Using the cosine rule: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C. c² = 49 + 64 - 2(7)(8)(0.5) = 113 - 56 = 57. Thus c = √57.
questions.p: We use cosine rule formula. When we calculate 49 plus 64 minus 56, we go get 57, so the side na √57.

questions.q: A ship sails 5 km due North and then 12 km due East. How far is the ship from the starting point?
questions.e: The movement forms a right-angled triangle with legs 5 and 12. The distance is the hypotenuse: √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13.
questions.p: This one na right-angle triangle. You just use Pythagoras to find the hypotenuse, which be √(25 + 144) = 13.

questions.q: What is the bearing of South-West from a point?
questions.e: North is 0 degrees, East is 90, South is 180, and West is 270. South-West is exactly halfway between 180 and 270, which is 180 + 45 = 225 degrees.
questions.p: South na 180 degrees and West na 270 degrees. South-West dey middle of the two, so 180 plus 45 give you 225 degrees.

questions.q: Find the value of 2 sin 30 degrees × cos 60 degrees.
questions.p: If you replace the values, you get 2 times 0.5 times 0.5. That one go give you 0.5.

questions.q: A ladder 13 meters long leans against a wall. If the foot of the ladder is 5 meters from the wall, what is the angle the ladder makes with the ground?
questions.e: The ladder is the hypotenuse (13m) and the distance from the wall is the adjacent side (5m). Cos theta = adjacent/hypotenuse = 5/13. Thus, theta = arccos(5/13).
questions.p: Ladder na the hypotenuse, and distance from wall na adjacent side. Since cos na adjacent over hypotenuse, angle theta go be arccos(5/13).

questions.q: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x³ - 5x² + 7x - 9 with respect to x.
questions.e: Apply the power rule to each term by multiplying by the power and reducing the power by 1. The derivative of 4x³ is 12x², -5x² becomes -10x, 7x becomes 7, and the constant -9 becomes 0.
questions.p: Just use power rule for each term. Multiply coefficient by power and reduce power by one. You go get 12x² - 10x + 7.

questions.q: Determine the gradient of the curve y = 3x² - 4x + 5 at the point where x = 2.
questions.e: First find the derivative dy/dx = 6x - 4 to represent the gradient function. Then substitute x = 2 into the derivative to get 6(2) - 4 = 12 - 4 = 8.
questions.p: Differentiate the equation to get dy/dx = 6x - 4. Put x = 2 inside am, you go get 12 minus 4, wey be 8.

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = x² + 3x at the point (1, 4).
questions.e: The slope of the tangent is the derivative dy/dx = 2x + 3 evaluated at x = 1, giving m = 5. Using the point-slope formula y - y1 = m(x - x1), we get y - 4 = 5(x - 1), which simplifies to y = 5x - 1.
questions.p: Find dy/dx wey be 2x + 3, put x = 1 to get slope m = 5. Use formula y - y1 = m(x - x1) to get y = 5x - 1.

questions.q: Find the values of x for which the function f(x) = x³ - 12x is increasing.
questions.e: A function is increasing when its derivative is greater than zero. f'(x) = 3x² - 12 > 0, which means x² > 4. Solving this inequality yields x < -2 or x > 2.
questions.p: Make function dey increase, f'(x) must pass zero. So 3x² - 12 > 0 meaning x² > 4, dat means x < -2 or x > 2.

questions.q: If the displacement of a particle at time t seconds is given by s(t) = t³ - 6t² + 9t + 4, find the acceleration of the particle when t = 2 seconds.
questions.e: Velocity is the first derivative v(t) = s'(t) = 3t² - 12t + 9. Acceleration is the second derivative a(t) = v'(t) = 6t - 12. Substituting t = 2 gives a(2) = 6(2) - 12 = 0 m/s².
questions.p: Velocity na first differentiation, acceleration na second one. Differentiate twice to get a(t) = 6t - 12. Put t = 2, you go get zero.

questions.q: Find the minimum value of the function f(x) = x² - 6x + 10.
questions.e: Find the critical point by setting f'(x) = 2x - 6 = 0, which gives x = 3. Substitute x = 3 back into the original function: f(3) = (3)² - 6(3) + 10 = 9 - 18 + 10 = 1.
questions.p: Differentiate and equate to zero to get x = 3. Put 3 inside the original equation, you go get 9 - 18 + 10, wey be 1.

questions.q: The radius of a circular oil spill on water is increasing at a constant rate of 2 cm/s. Find the rate at which the area of the spill is increasing when the radius is 5 cm.
questions.e: The area of a circle is A = π × r². Using the chain rule, dA/dt = (dA/dr) × (dr/dt) = (2pi × r) × (dr/dt). Substituting r = 5 and dr/dt = 2 gives dA/dt = (2pi × 5) × 2 = 20pi cm²/s.
questions.p: Area formula na A = π r². Use chain rule: dA/dt = 2 π r times dr/dt. Put r = 5 and dr/dt = 2, na 20pi you go get.

questions.q: At what value of x does the function f(x) = 2x³ - 15x² + 36x have a maximum value?
questions.e: First find f'(x) = 6x² - 30x + 36 = 0, giving x² - 5x + 6 = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3. The second derivative is f''(x) = 12x - 30. For x = 2, f''(2) = 24 - 30 = -6 (maximum since it's negative).
questions.p: Differentiate to get 6x² - 30x + 36 = 0, roots na x = 2 and x = 3. Use second derivative test, na x = 2 go give negative result, meaning maximum.

questions.q: Find the derivative of y = (3x² - 1)⁴ with respect to x.
questions.e: Apply the chain rule. Let u = 3x² - 1 so y = u⁴. Then dy/dx = 4u³ × (du/dx) = 4(3x² - 1)³ × (6x) = 24x(3x² - 1)³.
questions.p: Use chain rule. Bring power 4 come front, reduce power by 1, then multiply by differentiation of inside function (6x). Result na 24x(3x² - 1)³.

questions.q: Evaluate the indefinite integral: int (6x² - 4x + 5) dx.
questions.e: Integrate each term using the power rule by adding 1 to the exponent and dividing by the new exponent. This gives (6x³)/3 - (4x²)/2 + 5x + C, which simplifies to 2x³ - 2x² + 5x + C.
questions.p: Make you integrate each term one by one by adding one to the power and divide by that new power. When you cancel out, you go get 2x³ - 2x² + 5x + C.

questions.q: Find the definite integral: int_0² (3x² + 2) dx.
questions.e: The integral of 3x² + 2 is x³ + 2x. Evaluating this from 0 to 2 gives (2³ + 2(2)) - (0³ + 2(0)), which equals 8 + 4 = 12.
questions.p: Integration of 3x² + 2 na x³ + 2x. When you put 2 and 0 inside, you go get (8 + 4) minus zero, wey be 12.

questions.q: Evaluate the indefinite integral: int (3 / x²) dx.
questions.e: Rewrite 3/x² as 3x⁻². Applying the power rule gives 3x⁻¹/(-1) + C, which simplifies to -3/x + C.
questions.p: First turn 3/x² to 3x power minus 2. Apply power rule by adding one to power, e go give you -3/x + C.

questions.q: Find the value of k if int_0ᵏ (2x + 1) dx = 12, where k > 0.
questions.e: Integrating 2x + 1 gives [x² + x] evaluated from 0 to k, which is k² + k. Equating this to 12 gives k² + k - 12 = 0, so (k + 4)(k - 3) = 0, giving k = 3 since k > 0.
questions.p: If you integrate 2x + 1, you get x² + x. Make you equate k² + k to 12, solve quadratic equation, you go get k = 3 because k must positive.

questions.q: Evaluate: int (4 cos(2x)) dx.
questions.e: The integral of cos(ax) is (1/a) sin(ax). Therefore, int 4 cos(2x) dx = 4(1/2) sin(2x) + C = 2 sin(2x) + C.
questions.p: Integration of cos(2x) na half sin(2x). When you multiply am by 4, you go get 2 sin(2x) plus your constant C.

questions.q: Evaluate the indefinite integral: int e^(3x - 1) dx.
questions.e: The integral of e^(ax + b) is (1/a) e^(ax + b) + C. Here a = 3, so the result is (1/3)e^(3x - 1) + C.
questions.p: When you integrate exponential function like e^(3x - 1), you just divide by the coefficient of x, wey be 3. E go give you e^(3x - 1)/3 + C.

questions.q: Evaluate the definite integral: int_1ᵉ (1/x) dx.
questions.e: The integral of 1/x is ln|x|. Evaluating from 1 to e gives ln(e) - ln(1) = 1 - 0 = 1.
questions.p: Integration of 1/x na ln(x). When you put e and 1, ln(e) na 1 while ln(1) na 0, so 1 minus 0 na 1.

questions.q: Using integration by substitution or otherwise, evaluate: int 2x(x² + 5)³ dx.
questions.e: Let u = x² + 5, then du = 2x dx. The integral becomes int u³ du = u⁴ / 4 + C. Substituting back gives ((x² + 5)⁴)/4 + C.
questions.p: Make you let u = x² + 5, so du na 2x dx. The integral come turn to u³ du, wey give u⁴ over 4. Put your x back, you get ((x² + 5)⁴)/4 + C.

questions.q: What is the mode of the numbers: 5, 8, 5, 12, 7, 8, 5, 10, 3?
questions.e: The mode is the number that appears with the highest frequency in a given set of data. Counting the occurrences, 5 appears three times, which is more than any other number.
questions.p: Mode na that number wey dey show pass all of them inside the list. Na 5 repeat three times, so na 5 be the mode.

questions.q: Calculate the variance of the numbers 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10.
questions.e: First find the mean: (2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 10) / 5 = 6. Next, find the squared differences from the mean: (2-6)²=16, (4-6)²=4, (6-6)²=0, (8-6)²=4, (10-6)²=16. Sum of squares = 40, so variance = 40 / 5 = 8.
questions.p: First find the mean, wey be 6. Dem minus mean from each number and square am: 16, 4, 0, 4, 16, wey sum up to 40. Divide by 5 to get variance, which is 8.

questions.q: The mean of five numbers is 20. If one number is removed, the mean of the remaining four numbers becomes 17. Find the value of the removed number.
questions.e: Total sum of the 5 numbers = 5 × 20 = 100. Total sum of the remaining 4 numbers = 4 × 17 = 68. The value of the removed number is 100 - 68 = 32.
questions.p: Multiply the first mean by 5 to get total sum (100). Multiply the new mean by 4 to get the new sum (68). Minus the two sums to find the number wey commot, na 100 minus 68 = 32.

questions.q: What is the standard deviation of the set of numbers: 3, 3, 3, 3, 3?
questions.e: All the values in the data set are identical. Since there is no deviation or spread from the mean, the standard deviation is 0.
questions.p: All the numbers na the same thing. Since nobody dey scatter or waka different from the mean, standard deviation must be zero.

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, the mean score in a physics test was 65. If the mean score of the 25 girls was 70, find the mean score of the boys.
questions.e: Total score for all 40 students = 40 × 65 = 2600. Total score for 25 girls = 25 × 70 = 1750. Total score for the 15 boys = 2600 - 1750 = 850. Mean for boys = 850 / 15 = 56.67, which rounds to 56.7.
questions.p: Find total score for everybody (40 times 65 = 2600). Find total for girls (25 times 70 = 1750). Minus am to get boys' total (850), then divide by number of boys (15) to get 56.7.

questions.q: Find the standard deviation of the numbers 1, 4, and 7.
questions.e: Mean = (1 + 4 + 7) / 3 = 4. Squared deviations from mean: (1-4)² = 9, (4-4)² = 0, (7-4)² = 9. Variance = (9 + 0 + 9) / 3 = 18 / 3 = 6. Standard deviation = √6.
questions.p: Find mean, e give you 4. Minus 4 from each number and square am: 9, 0, 9. Add dem together divide by 3 to get variance (6). Put am inside square root to get √6.

questions.q: The mean of ten positive numbers is 15. If each number is multiplied by 2 and then increased by 5, what is the new mean?
questions.e: When every value in a data set is multiplied by a constant a and has a constant b added to it, the new mean is simply a × (old mean) + b. Therefore, new mean = 2 × 15 + 5 = 30 + 5 = 35.
questions.p: If you multiply every number by 2 and add 5, your mean go follow do the exact same thing. Just multiply the old mean by 2 and add 5: (2 times 15) + 5 = 35.

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word KANO be arranged?
questions.e: The word KANO has 4 distinct letters. The number of arrangements is given by 4 factorial (4!), which is 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24.
questions.p: The word KANO get 4 different letters wey no repeat. To arrange dem, na 4 factorial (4!), wey mean 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 wey give 24.

questions.q: Find the value of n if P(n, 2) = 30.
questions.e: P(n, 2) means n(n - 1) = 30. Solving the quadratic equation n² - n - 30 = 0 gives (n - 6)(n + 5) = 0, so n = 6 since n must be positive.
questions.p: P(n, 2) mean say n(n - 1) = 30. If you solve am, you go get n² - n - 30 = 0, wey fit factorize to (n - 6)(n + 5) = 0. E con remain n = 6.

questions.q: Evaluate C(7, 3).
questions.p: To calculate C(7, 3), na 7 factorial divide by 3 factorial times 4 factorial. Dat na (7 x 6 x 5) / (3 x 2 x 1) wey give 35.

questions.q: If C(n, 4) = C(n, 2), find the value of n.
questions.e: Using the combination property C(n, a) = C(n, b) implies either a = b or a + b = n. Since 4 does not equal 2, we have 4 + 2 = n, so n = 6.
questions.p: If C(n, a) = C(n, b), e mean say na either a = b abi a + b = n. Since 4 no be 2, na 4 + 2 = n, so nna 6.

questions.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 2, 3, 5, 7, and 8 if repetition of digits is not allowed?
questions.e: There are 5 available digits and we need to choose and arrange 3 of them. This is P(5, 3) = 5 x 4 x 3 = 60.
questions.p: We get 5 numbers and we wan arrange 3 of dem where repetition no dey allowed. Na permutation P(5, 3), wey be 5 x 4 x 3 = 60.

questions.q: In how many ways can a committee of 3 men and 2 women be chosen from 5 men and 4 women?
questions.e: Choose 3 men from 5 in C(5, 3) ways, and 2 women from 4 in C(4, 2) ways. Total ways = C(5, 3) x C(4, 2) = 10 x 6 = 60.
questions.p: Pick 3 men out of 5 na C(5, 3) = 10, and pick 2 women out of 4 na C(4, 2) = 6. Multiply dem together, 10 x 6 = 60.

questions.q: Find the number of distinct arrangements of the letters of the word LAGOS.
questions.e: The word LAGOS has 5 distinct letters with no repetition. The number of arrangements is 5! = 120.
questions.p: The word LAGOS get 5 letters and none dey repeat. So na 5 factorial (5!), wey be 120.

questions.q: In a class of 10 students, in how many ways can a captain and a vice-captain be appointed?
questions.e: Since the positions of captain and vice-captain are distinct (order matters), we use permutation P(10, 2) = 10 x 9 = 90.
questions.p: Because captain and vice-captain different, order matter well well. Na permutation P(10, 2), wey be 10 x 9 = 90.

questions.q: A box contains 4 red balls and 3 blue balls. In how many ways can 3 balls be drawn such that at least 2 are red?
questions.e: At least 2 red means either (2 red and 1 blue) or (3 red and 0 blue). Calculation: C(4, 2) x C(3, 1) + C(4, 3) x C(3, 0) = (6 x 3) + (4 x 1) = 18 + 4 = 22.
questions.p: At least 2 red mean say na either 2 red and 1 blue, abi all 3 red. Dat na [C(4, 2) x C(3, 1)] + [C(4, 3) x C(3, 0)] = 18 + 4 = 22.

questions.q: Find the number of ways 5 people can sit around a circular table.
questions.e: The number of circular permutations for n objects is (n - 1)!. For 5 people, it is (5 - 1)! = 4! = 24.
questions.p: When people dey sit round circle table, the formula na (n - 1)!. For 5 people, na (5 - 1)! wey be 4! = 24.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 blue marbles, 3 red marbles, and 2 green marbles. If a marble is picked at random, what is the probability that it is NOT red?
questions.e: Total marbles = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10. The number of marbles that are not red is 5 (blue) + 2 (green) = 7. Therefore, the probability is 7/10.
questions.p: Total marbles na 5 + 3 + 2 = 10. Marbles wey no be red na 5 blue plus 2 green, wey be 7. So, the probability na 7/10.

questions.q: A fair die is tossed twice. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers obtained is exactly 7?
questions.e: The total outcomes when tossing two dice is 6 × 6 = 36. The pairs that sum to 7 are (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), and (6,1), which are 6 pairs. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.
questions.p: Total way two dice fit fall na 36. The pairs wey go add join reach 7 na 6: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), and (6,1). Probability na 6 divide by 36, wey be 1/6.

questions.q: Two unbiased coins are tossed once. What is the probability of obtaining at least one head?
questions.e: The sample space is {HH, HT, TH, TT}. Outcomes with at least one head are {HH, HT, TH}, which are 3 out of 4 possible outcomes.
questions.p: Possibilities na {HH, HT, TH, TT}. The ones wey get at least one head na {HH, HT, TH}. That one na 3 out of 4.

questions.q: A box contains 4 white, 6 black, and x red balls. If the probability of picking a black ball is 0.3, find the value of x.
questions.e: Total balls = 4 + 6 + x = 10 + x. Probability of black = 6 / (10 + x) = 0.3. So, 6 = 0.3(10 + x), which means 6 = 3 + 0.3x. Solving gives 3 = 0.3x, so x = 10.
questions.p: Total balls na 10 + x. Probability say you pick black na 6 divide by (10 + x). We know say dis one equal to 0.3. If you solve the equation, x go be 10.

questions.q: What is the probability that a day chosen at random from the days of the week begins with the letter 'T'?
questions.e: The days of the week are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. The days starting with T are Tuesday and Thursday. So, 2/7.
questions.p: Days wey start with T for week na Tuesday and Thursday. Total days na 7, so the probability na 2 over 7.

questions.q: A box contains 3 red pens and 2 blue pens. Two pens are picked one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both pens are red?
questions.e: Probability of first red = 3/5. Since it is without replacement, the probability of second red = 2/4. Total probability = 3/5 × 2/4 = 6/20 = 3/10.
questions.p: First time you pick red, e be 3/5. Because you no return the pen, the second red go remain 2/4. Multiply them together, you go get 3/10.

questions.q: If the probability of an event E is 0.65, what is the probability of the complement of the event, E'?
questions.e: The sum of probabilities of an event and its complement is 1. Therefore, P(E') = 1 - P(E) = 1 - 0.65 = 0.35.
questions.p: Total probability must be 1. So if E na 0.65, the one wey no happen (E') go be 1 minus 0.65, wey be 0.35.

questions.q: A bag has 10 tickets numbered 1 to 10. If one ticket is drawn, what is the probability that the number on the ticket is a prime number?
questions.e: Prime numbers between 1 and 10 are 2, 3, 5, 7. There are 4 prime numbers. Probability = 4/10 = 2/5.
questions.p: Prime numbers between 1 and 10 na 2, 3, 5, and 7. Total count na 4. So the probability na 4 over 10, wey be 2/5.

questions.q: A spinner is divided into 8 equal sectors colored red, blue, and yellow. There are 4 red, 3 blue, and 1 yellow sector. What is the probability of the spinner landing on blue or yellow?
questions.e: Probability of blue = 3/8. Probability of yellow = 1/8. Probability of blue or yellow = 3/8 + 1/8 = 4/8 = 1/2.
questions.p: Probability say e go land on blue na 3/8, and yellow na 1/8. Because you want any of the two, you add them together, e go give you 4/8, wey be 1/2.

questions.q: Convert the binary number 101101 (base 2) to base 10.
questions.e: 101101 in base 2 means 1x32 + 0x16 + 1x8 + 1x4 + 0x2 + 1x1 = 32+8+4+1 = 45. So the base 10 value is 45.

questions.q: Multiply 23 (base 5) by 3 (base 5), leaving your answer in base 5.
questions.e: 23 base 5 = 2x5+3 = 13 in base 10, and 3 base 5 = 3. Multiplying gives 13 x 3 = 39. Converting 39 back to base 5: 39 = 1x25 + 2x5 + 4, so the answer is 124 base 5.
questions.p: 23 for base 5 na 2x5+3 = 13 for base 10, and 3 base 5 na 3. 13 x 3 = 39. If you convert 39 go back to base 5: 39 = 1x25 + 2x5 + 4, e be 124 base 5.

questions.q: In a certain base x, the number 341 (base x) is equal to 133 in base ten. Find the value of x.
questions.e: 341 base x means 3x² + 4x + 1. Setting this equal to 133 gives 3x² + 4x - 132 = 0. Using the quadratic formula, the discriminant is 16 + 1584 = 1600, √1600 = 40, so x = (-4+40)/6 = 6.
questions.p: 341 for base x mean 3x² + 4x + 1. If you set am equal to 133, you go get 3x² + 4x - 132 = 0. Solve am with quadratic formula, discriminant na 16+1584=1600, √ na 40, so x = (-4+40)/6 = 6.

questions.q: Evaluate 101011 (base 2) minus 1101 (base 2), leaving your answer in base 2.
questions.e: 101011 base 2 = 32+8+2+1 = 43 in base 10, and 1101 base 2 = 8+4+1 = 13. So 43 - 13 = 30. Converting 30 back to base 2 gives 16+8+4+2 = 11110 base 2.
questions.p: 101011 for base 2 na 32+8+2+1 = 43 for base 10, and 1101 base 2 na 8+4+1 = 13. So 43 - 13 = 30. If you convert 30 go back to base 2, e be 16+8+4+2 = 11110 base 2.

questions.q: Evaluate 2/5 + 1/4, leaving your answer as a decimal.
questions.p: 2/5 be 0.4 and 1/4 be 0.25. If you add dem together, 0.4 + 0.25 go give 0.65.

questions.q: Amina's monthly salary was increased from ₦45,000 to ₦54,000. What was the percentage increase in her salary?
questions.p: The increase na 54,000 - 45,000 = 9,000. To find percentage, you do (9,000/45,000) x 100 = 20%.

questions.q: A trader bought goods worth ₦8,000. He sold 3/4 of the goods at a profit of 25% and the remaining 1/4 at a loss of 10%. Find his overall percentage profit on the whole transaction.
questions.e: Cost of 3/4 portion = N6,000, sold at 25% profit = N7,500. Cost of 1/4 portion = N2,000, sold at 10% loss = N1,800. Total selling price = N9,300, so profit = N1,300. Percentage profit = (1,300/8,000) x 100 = 16.25%.
questions.p: 3/4 of the goods cost N6,000, e sell am for 25% profit wey be N7,500. The remaining 1/4 cost N2,000, e sell am for 10% loss wey be N1,800. Total money wey e get na N9,300, so profit na N1,300, wey be (1,300/8,000) x 100 = 16.25%.

questions.q: Evaluate 7⁰ + 4^(1/2).
questions.e: Any non-zero number raised to power 0 is 1, so 7⁰ = 1. Also 4^(1/2) means square root of 4, which is 2. Adding them gives 1 + 2 = 3.
questions.p: Any number wey get power zero na 1, so 7⁰ = 1. 4^(1/2) na square root of 4, wey be 2. If you add am, 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.q: Simplify x⁵ × x⁻² ÷ x⁻³, where x is not equal to zero.
questions.e: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the indices: 5 + (-2) = 3. Dividing by x⁻³ means subtracting (-3), which is the same as adding 3, so 3 + 3 = 6. This gives x⁶.

questions.q: If 5ʸ⁺³ = 125², find the value of y.
questions.e: Write 125 as 5³, so 125² becomes (5³)² = 5⁶. Since the bases are equal, the powers must be equal: y + 3 = 6, so y = 3.

questions.q: Given that log₁₀(5) = 0.6990, find the value of log₁₀(20).

questions.q: Simplify √45, leaving your answer in the form k × √5.

questions.q: Which of the following surds is a rational number?
questions.e: √121 = 11 because 121 is a perfect square (11 × 11 = 121), so it is rational. The numbers 98, 72, and 50 are not perfect squares, so their square roots stay irrational.
questions.p: √121 = 11 because 121 na perfect square (11 times 11 = 121), so e be rational number. 98, 72, and 50 no be perfect square, so their square roots remain irrational.

questions.q: Evaluate (√8 + √18) × √2.
questions.e: √8 = 2sqrt(2) and √18 = 3sqrt(2). Adding gives 2sqrt(2) + 3sqrt(2) = 5sqrt(2). Multiplying by √2 gives 5 × 2 = 10.

questions.q: In a class of 45 students in a secondary school in Enugu, every student offers at least one of Mathematics or English Language. If 28 students offer Mathematics and 22 offer English Language, how many students offer Mathematics only?
questions.e: Since every student offers at least one subject, n(M union E) = 45. Using n(M)+n(E)-n(M and E) = n(M union E): 28+22-n(M and E)=45, so n(M and E) = 5. Mathematics only = 28 - 5 = 23.
questions.p: Since na at least one subject every student take, n(M union E) = 45. From 28+22-n(M and E)=45, we get n(M and E) = 5. So Maths only = 28 - 5 = 23.

questions.q: In a survey of traders at Onitsha main market, 50 sell Garri, 40 sell Beans, and 35 sell Rice. Among these, 15 sell both Garri and Beans, 12 sell both Beans and Rice, 10 sell both Garri and Rice, and 5 sell all three products. How many traders sell exactly two of the three products?
questions.e: Exactly two products means subtracting those in all three from each pair overlap: (Garri and Beans only) = 15-5=10, (Beans and Rice only) = 12-5=7, (Garri and Rice only) = 10-5=5. Adding these: 10+7+5 = 22.

questions.q: In a two-set Venn diagram, U is the universal set shown as a rectangle, with two overlapping circles A and B drawn inside it. Which set notation correctly describes the region that lies outside both circles A and B, but is still inside the rectangle representing U?
questions.e: The region outside both circles is the complement of their union, written as (A union B)'. By De Morgan's law, (A union B)' = A' intersection B', which describes the area outside both A and B but still within U.
questions.p: The part wey dey outside the two circles na the complement of their union, (A union B)'. By De Morgan law, (A union B)' = A' intersection B', wey be the area wey no dey inside A or B but e still dey inside U.

questions.p: Sale from the 30 bags wey get profit = 30 x 18000 x 1.10 = ₦594,000. Sale from the 20 bags wey get loss = 20 x 18000 x 0.95 = ₦342,000. Total sale = ₦936,000, profit be 936000 - 900000 = ₦36,000, wey be 4% of the ₦900,000 wey she spend.

questions.p: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T, so 242000 = P x (1.1)² = P x 1.21. If you divide 242000 by 1.21, you go get P = ₦200,000.

questions.p: Since F dey vary as t², we get F = k × t². We use 50 = k × 25 to find k = 2. When t = 8, F = 2 × 64 = 128.

questions.q: The time T taken by Chidinma to drive from Enugu to Onitsha varies inversely as her average speed S. If T = 3 hours when S = 60 km/h, find T when S = 90 km/h.

questions.p: T dey vary inverse to S, so T × S = k. From T=3, S=60, we get k=180. When S=90, T = 180/90 = 2 hours.

questions.q: The cost C of tiling a rectangular floor varies jointly as its length L and its breadth B. It costs ₦9000 to tile a floor that is 6 metres long and 3 metres wide. Find the cost of tiling a floor that is 8 metres long and 5 metres wide.

questions.p: C dey vary jointly as L and B, so C = kLB. From 9000 = k × 6 × 3, we get k = 500. For L=8, B=5: C = 500 × 8 × 5 = 20000.

questions.q: The total cost C (in naira) of producing x bags of garri is partly constant and partly varies directly as x. When x = 10, C = ₦7000, and when x = 20, C = ₦12000. Find the cost of producing 15 bags.

questions.q: At a stationery shop in Kano, Musa bought 3 pencils and 2 pens for ₦370, while Ngozi bought 2 pencils and 3 pens for ₦380. What is the cost of one pen?
questions.e: Let pencil = p, pen = q: 3p+2q=370 and 2p+3q=380. Multiply the first by 2 and second by 3, then subtract to eliminate p: 5q = 400, so q = 80. One pen costs ₦80.
questions.p: Make pencil be p, pen be q: 3p+2q=370 and 2p+3q=380. If you multiply first by 2, second by 3, then minus am, you go get 5q = 400, so q = 80. One pen na ₦80.

questions.e: From x - y = 2, x = y + 2. Put this into 3x+2y=16: 3(y+2)+2y=16, so 5y=10, y=2, x=4. Then 2x - y = 8 - 2 = 6.
questions.p: From x - y = 2, x = y + 2. Put am enter 3x+2y=16: 3(y+2)+2y=16, so 5y=10, y=2, x=4. Then 2x - y = 8 - 2 = 6.

questions.q: A trader's record shows that the cost of 4 bags of rice and 3 bags of beans is ₦152,000, while the cost of 2 bags of rice and 5 bags of beans is ₦160,000. Find the cost of one bag of rice.

questions.q: If alpha and beta are the roots of 2x² - 9x + 4 = 0, find the quadratic equation whose roots are 1/alpha and 1/beta.

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, meaning all four points A, B, C and D lie on the circumference of the same circle, with the vertices taken in that order round the circle. If angle A (angle DAB) is 108°, what is the size of angle C (angle BCD), the angle opposite to angle A?

questions.q: In a circle with centre O, two tangents are drawn from an external point T, touching the circle at points A and B. If OA = 5 cm (the radius) and OT = 13 cm (the distance from the centre to the external point), what is the length of the tangent TA?
