questions.e: Multiply 0.8125 by 2 repeatedly: 0.8125x2=1.625 (1), 0.625x2=1.25 (1), 0.25x2=0.5 (0), 0.5x2=1.0 (1). Reading the bits gives 0.1101 in base 2.
questions.p: To convert decimal fractions to base 2, you dey multiply am by 2 and pick the whole numbers. If you multiply 0.8125 by 2 repeatedly, you go get 1, 1, 0, and 1. When you read am from top to bottom, e go give you 0.1101.

questions.q: If 23_x = 17 in base 10, find the base x.
questions.e: 23 in base x means 2x + 3 = 17, so 2x = 14 and x = 7. Checking, 23 in base 7 equals 2x7+3 = 17, which confirms the base.
questions.p: To find the unknown base, you expand 23 in base x as 2x + 3 and equate am to 17. When you solve 2x = 14, you go get x = 7. E dey correct because 2 times 7 plus 3 na 17.

questions.q: A number in base 4 is given as 132₄. Find the value of this number when expressed in base 5.
questions.e: First convert 132 base 4 to base 10: (1x16) + (3x4) + 2 = 16 + 12 + 2 = 30. Converting 30 to base 5 gives 110, since 1x25 + 1x5 + 0 = 30.
questions.p: First, make you change 132 base 4 to base 10, wey give us 30. Then, convert that 30 to base 5, e go give you 110.

questions.q: A trader estimated the length of a piece of cloth as 15.6 m, but the actual length was 15.0 m. Find the percentage error in his estimate, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.e: Percentage error = (error/actual value) × 100 = (0.6/15.0) × 100 = 4.0%.
questions.p: To find percentage error, you go divide error by actual value and multiply by 100. Dis one give us (0.6 / 15.0) × 100, wey come out to 4.0%.

questions.q: In a school election, 60% of the 450 registered voters voted for Musa, and the rest voted for Kemi. How many more votes did Musa get than Kemi?
questions.e: Musa got 60% of 450 = 270 votes, Kemi got 40% of 450 = 180 votes. The difference is 270 - 180 = 90.
questions.p: Musa carry 60% of 450, wey be 270 votes, while Kemi carry the remaining 40%, wey be 180 votes. When you subtract 180 from 270, you go get 90.

questions.q: Convert the recurring decimal 0.4545454545... (0.45 recurring) to a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.p: If you make x equal to 0.4545..., 100x go be 45.4545... When you minus x from 100x, you get 99x = 45, and if you reduce am, e go give you 5/11.

questions.q: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₦2,500 and wants to mark it up so that after giving a 20% discount on the marked price, he still makes a profit of 15% on his cost price. What should the marked price be?
questions.e: Selling price needed = 115% of 2500 = ₦2,875. If marked price is M, then 80% of M = 2875, so M = 2875/0.8 = ₦3,593.75.
questions.p: To get 15% profit, selling price suppose be 115% of ₦2,500, wey be ₦2,875. Since dis selling price na 80% of marked price because of 20% discount, you divide ₦2,875 by 0.8 to get ₦3,593.75.

questions.q: Evaluate, correct to 3 significant figures, the value of (2.67 + 3.148)/0.25
questions.e: Adding gives 5.818, and dividing by 0.25 gives 23.272, which rounds to 3 significant figures as 23.3.
questions.p: If you add 2.67 and 3.148, you go get 5.818. When you divide that 5.818 by 0.25, you go get 23.272, wey be 23.3 when you round am to 3 significant figures.

questions.q: The population of a small town is given as 284,750. Express this number correct to 2 significant figures.
questions.e: To 2 significant figures, only the first two digits (2 and 8) are kept and the rest replaced by zeros. The third digit, 4, rounds down, giving 280,000.
questions.p: To write 284,750 to 2 significant figures, you only keep the first two numbers, 2 and 8. Because the third number na 4, you go round down, so you go get 280,000.

questions.q: A measuring instrument gives the length of a table as 1.25 m, correct to 2 decimal places. Between what limits does the actual length lie?
questions.e: A value rounded to 2 decimal places can be off by at most half of the last place value, which is 0.005. So the true length lies between 1.25 - 0.005 and 1.25 + 0.005, that is 1.245 m and 1.255 m.
questions.p: If you round to 2 decimal places, the error fit reach 0.005. So you go subtract and add 0.005 to 1.25 to get the range, wey be 1.245 m and 1.255 m.

questions.q: Tunde's score in a test increased from 48 to 60 out of 80 marks in two different tests. By what percentage did his score increase?
questions.e: The increase in score is 60 - 48 = 12. Percentage increase is (12/48) x 100 = 25%.
questions.p: The score increase from 48 to 60, so the difference na 12. To get the percentage, you divide 12 by 48 and multiply by 100, wey give you 25%.

questions.q: In a village of 2,400 people, 45% are children, 1/3 of the remainder are elderly, and the rest are working adults. How many working adults are there in the village?
questions.e: Children are 45% of 2400 = 1080, leaving 1320. Elderly are 1/3 of 1320 = 440, leaving working adults as 1320 - 440 = 880.
questions.p: Children na 1080, so 1320 people remain. One-third of that 1320 na 440 elderly people, so if you remove them, you go get 880 working adults.

questions.q: Simplify: (3/5 of 2/3) + (1/4 divided by 1/2), expressing the answer as a single fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.e: 3/5 of 2/3 equals 2/5. Dividing 1/4 by 1/2 equals 1/2. Adding 2/5 and 1/2 using a common denominator of 10 gives 4/10 + 5/10 = 9/10.
questions.p: 3/5 of 2/3 na 2/5, and 1/4 divide by 1/2 na 1/2. When you add 2/5 and 1/2 together, you go get 4/10 plus 5/10, wey be 9/10.

questions.q: Simplify: 2⁻³ × 2⁵
questions.e: Add the powers since the bases are the same: -3 + 5 = 2, so 2⁻³ × 2⁵ = 2² = 4.
questions.p: Make you add the powers sake of say the base numbers dey the same, so -3 + 5 na 2. E come mean say 2⁻³ × 2⁵ = 2², wey give us 4.

questions.e: A negative power means take the reciprocal, so (1/16)^(-1/4) = 16^(1/4). Since 16 = 2⁴, the fourth root of 16 is 2.
questions.p: Minus power mean make you turn am upside down, so (1/16)^(-1/4) come be 16^(1/4). Since 16 na 2⁴, the fourth root of 16 na 2.

questions.q: If a^(2/3) = 25, find the value of a, where a is positive.
questions.e: Raise both sides to the power 3/2: a = 25^(3/2) = (√25)³ = 5³ = 125.
questions.p: Raise both sides to the power of 3/2, so a = 25^(3/2). If you find the square root of 25 first, you get 5, and 5 power 3 na 125.

questions.q: Find the value of x if 2³ˣ = 1/8
questions.e: Write 1/8 as 2⁻³. Since the bases are equal, 3x = -3, so x = -1.
questions.p: Make you write 1/8 as 2⁻³. Because the base numbers match, na to equate the powers: 3x = -3, and when you divide, x = -1.

questions.q: A trader doubles her capital every year. If her capital after t years is given by C = ₦50,000 × 2ᵗ, how many years will it take for her capital to reach ₦1,600,000?
questions.e: Divide both sides by 50,000: 2ᵗ = 32. Since 32 = 2⁵, t = 5 years.
questions.p: Divide both sides by 50,000 make 2ᵗ stand alone, wey give you 32. Since 32 na the same thing as 2⁵, it means t = 5 years.

questions.q: Simplify: (2⁵ × 2³) / 2⁴
questions.e: Add the exponents on top: 5 + 3 = 8, giving 2⁸, then subtract the bottom exponent: 8 - 4 = 4, so the answer is 2⁴.
questions.p: Add the powers for up: 5 + 3 na 8, wey give us 2⁸. Then minus the bottom power from am, 8 - 4 na 4, so answer na 2⁴.

questions.q: If p^(-2/3) = 1/9, find the value of p, where p is positive.
questions.e: p^(-2/3) = 1/9 means p^(2/3) = 9. Raise both sides to the power 3/2: p = 9^(3/2) = (√9)³ = 3³ = 27.
questions.p: If p^(-2/3) = 1/9, e mean say p^(2/3) = 9. Make you raise both sides to power 3/2 to get p = 27.

questions.q: Given that 2ˣ = 5 and 2ʸ = 3, find the value of 2^(x+y).
questions.e: By the law of indices, 2^(x+y) = 2ˣ × 2ʸ. Substituting the given values: 2ˣ times 2ʸ equals 5 times 3, which is 15.
questions.p: According to law of indices, 2^(x+y) be like say you multiply 2ˣ and 2ʸ together. Just multiply 5 and 3 to get 15.

questions.e: Add the exponents in the numerator: 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, then subtract 1/4 from the result: 5/6 - 1/4 = 10/12 - 3/12 = 7/12, so the answer is a^(7/12).
questions.p: Add the powers for up: 1/2 + 1/3 na 5/6. Then minus 1/4 from am to get 7/12, so the answer na a^(7/12).

questions.q: Chidinma invests money such that her savings S after n months is given by S = 2000 × 3ⁿ naira. If her savings after n months is ₦54,000, find n.
questions.e: Set 2000 × 3ⁿ = 54000, so 3ⁿ = 27. Since 27 = 3³, n must equal 3.
questions.p: Divide 54000 by 2000 to get 3ⁿ = 27. Since 27 na 3³, n must be 3.

questions.q: Simplify completely: (25ⁿ × 5^(1-2n)) / 5ⁿ⁻³
questions.e: Write 25ⁿ as 5²ⁿ, so the numerator becomes 5^(2n+1-2n) = 5¹. Dividing by 5ⁿ⁻³ gives 5^(1-(n-3)) = 5^(4-n).
questions.p: Change 25ⁿ to 5²ⁿ so everything go carry base 5. Simplify the powers make you get 5^(4-n).

questions.q: Evaluate log₅(1/125).
questions.e: 1/125 = 5⁻³, so log base 5 of 1/125 equals -3. This uses the rule that log of a reciprocal power gives a negative exponent.
questions.p: Since 1/125 na 5⁻³, the log base 5 go give us -3. Na simple rule of indices we use here.

questions.q: Simplify: log_a(a³) + log_a(1), where a is greater than 0 and not equal to 1.
questions.e: log_a(a³) equals 3 because the base and the power match, and log_a(1) is always 0 for any valid base. Adding these gives 3 + 0 = 3.
questions.p: Log_a(a³) na 3 because the base and power match. Since log_a(1) always be 0, 3 plus 0 give us 3.

questions.q: Given that log₁₀(3) = 0.4771, evaluate log₁₀(1/9) correct to 4 decimal places.
questions.e: 1/9 = 3⁻², so log₁₀(1/9) = -2 log₁₀(3) = -2(0.4771) = -0.9542. The negative sign shows the value is less than 1.
questions.p: We know say 1/9 na 3⁻², so we multiply -2 by 0.4771. The answer come out -0.9542.

questions.q: Express log₁₀(a² × b / c³) in terms of log₁₀(a), log₁₀(b) and log₁₀(c).
questions.e: Using the laws of logarithms, multiplication becomes addition and division becomes subtraction, while powers move to the front as multipliers. This gives 2log_10(a) + log₁₀(b) minus 3log_10(c).
questions.p: We use log laws where multiplication turn to addition and division turn to subtraction. The powers come front as multiplier, so we get 2log_10(a) + log₁₀(b) - 3log_10(c).

questions.q: If log₁₀(x) = 2.4771 and log₁₀(3) = 0.4771, find the value of x.
questions.e: Since log₁₀(x) = 2 + 0.4771, this can be split as log₁₀(100) + log₁₀(3) = log₁₀(300). Therefore x equals 300.
questions.p: We split 2.4771 into 2 plus 0.4771. Since 2 na log₁₀(100), we multiply 100 by 3 to get 300.

questions.q: Chidinma was asked to arrange the following surds in ascending order of magnitude: 2√3, 3√2, √15. Which arrangement is correct?
questions.e: Squaring each gives 2√3 = 12, √15 = 15, 3√2 = 18. So in ascending order: 2√3, √15, 3√2.
questions.p: If you put everything inside square root, 2√3 go be √12, 3√2 go be √18, and √15 remain √15. As we dey arrange am from small to big, e go be 2√3, √15, then 3√2.

questions.q: Simplify (√5 + √3)²
questions.e: Expand using (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b²: 5 + 2√15 + 3 = 8 + 2√15.
questions.p: Make you expand am using the formula (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b². E go give you 5 + 2√15 + 3, and when you add the numbers join, you go get 8 + 2√15.

questions.q: Rationalize the denominator of 6 / (2√3 - √2), leaving your answer in simplest surd form
questions.e: Multiply top and bottom by (2√3 + √2): denominator becomes 12 - 2 = 10, numerator becomes 6(2√3+√2) = 12√3 + 6√2. This gives (12√3 + 6√2)/10.
questions.p: Multiply both up and down by (2√3 + √2). The down part go give you 12 - 2 wey be 10, and the up part go give you 12√3 + 6√2.

questions.q: A rectangular farmland owned by Alhaji Musa has length (√8 + √2) metres and width √2 metres. Find the area of the farmland in square metres.
questions.e: Area = (√8 + √2) x √2 = √16 + √4 = 4 + 2 = 6 square metres.
questions.p: To find area, multiply length by width which be (√8 + √2) times √2. E go give you √16 + √4, and since √16 na 4 and √4 na 2, everything come add up give you 6.

questions.e: Combine over a common denominator: the denominator (√3-1)(√3+1) = 2, and the numerator (√3+1)² + (√3-1)² = 8. So the expression equals 8/2 = 4.
questions.p: If you use common denominator, the down part (√3-1)(√3+1) go give you 2, and the up part go give you 8. When you divide 8 by 2, your answer na 4.

questions.q: Simplify: √2/√8
questions.e: √2/√8 = √(2/8) = √(1/4) = 1/2. This is a basic surd simplification using division under one root.
questions.p: If you put √2 and √8 inside one root, e go give you √(1/4). When you find the root, e go come out as 1/2.

questions.q: Express 7 + 4sqrt(3) in the form (a + b)² where a and b are surds or whole numbers, hence find √(7 + 4sqrt(3)).
questions.e: We want (a+b)² = a²+b²+2ab = 7+4sqrt(3), so a²+b²=7 and 2ab=4sqrt(3) meaning ab=2sqrt(3). Taking a=2, b=√3 gives a²+b²=4+3=7, which works, so √(7+4sqrt(3)) = 2+√3.
questions.p: We find two numbers wey their sum na 7 and their product na 12, con use am split 4sqrt(3) to get 2 and √3. When we take the root, we get 2 + √3.

questions.q: A square flower bed in a school garden in Enugu has an area of (12 + 2sqrt(35)) square metres. If the side length can be written as √a + √b where a and b are positive integers with a > b, find the value of a + b.
questions.e: If side = √a + √b, then area = a + b + 2sqrt(ab). Comparing with 12 + 2sqrt(35): a + b = 12 and ab = 35, giving a=7, b=5. So a + b = 12.
questions.p: Area of square na side squared, wey match with a + b + 2sqrt(ab). Since a + b = 12 directly from the question, na 12 be our answer.

questions.q: If 2sqrt(3) + 5sqrt(3) - ksqrt(3) = 3sqrt(3), find the value of k.
questions.e: Combine like surd terms: (2 + 5 - k)√3 = 3sqrt(3), so 7 - k = 3, giving k = 4.
questions.p: Make we join all the surds together, we go get (7 - k)√3 = 3sqrt(3). If we solve am, k go give us 4.

questions.q: Simplify (√6 + √2) / √2, leaving your answer in simplest surd form.
questions.e: Divide each term by √2: √6/√2 = √3 and √2/√2 = 1, so the expression simplifies to √3 + 1.
questions.p: Make we divide both √6 and √2 by √2. E go give us √3 plus 1.

questions.q: A ladder leans against a wall such that its length is represented as (√50 + √2) metres. Express this length in the form ksqrt(2) metres.
questions.e: √50 = 5sqrt(2), so √50 + √2 = 5sqrt(2) + √2 = 6sqrt(2) metres.
questions.p: First, simplify √50 to 5sqrt(2). When you add am to the remaining √2, everything go come out as 6sqrt(2).

questions.q: Given two sets A and B, which of the following Venn diagram shadings correctly represents the symmetric difference A delta B (elements in A or B but not in both)?
o: The region where circles A and B overlap only
Both circles A and B fully shaded, including their overlap
The parts of circles A and B that do not overlap, with the overlapping region left unshaded
The area outside both circles but inside the universal set
questions.e: Symmetric difference contains elements belonging to exactly one of the sets, so the overlapping middle part is excluded while the two outer parts are shaded. This matches the description of the non-overlapping parts of both circles.
questions.p: Symmetric difference mean say na only elements wey dey inside A or B we go take, but we no go touch the middle part. So, we go shade the two sides wey no join together.

questions.q: Let U be the set of all students in a class, with n(U) = 40. Let A be students who play chess and B be students who play draughts, where n(A) = 22, n(B) = 18, and n(A union B) = 30. How many students play neither chess nor draughts?
questions.e: Students playing neither game are found by subtracting the union from the universal set total: 40 - 30 = 10. This uses the basic complement rule for two sets.
questions.p: To find those wey no play any game, you just subtract the union from the total number of students. So, 40 minus 30 give us 10 students.

questions.q: A trader bought an article for ₦8,000 and sold it for ₦9,200. Find the percentage profit.
questions.e: Profit = 9200 - 8000 = 1200. Percentage profit = 1200/8000 x 100 = 15%.
questions.p: To find di profit, minus 8000 from 9200 to get 1200. Divide 1200 by 8000 and multiply by 100 to get 15%.

questions.q: Bola sells a table for ₦46,000, thereby making a profit of 15%. What was the cost price of the table?
questions.e: Let cost price be C. Then 1.15C = 46000, so C = 46000/1.15 = 40000. This is a straightforward reverse profit calculation.
questions.p: Make di cost price be C. Multiply 1.15 by C to get 46000, then divide 46000 by 1.15 to get 40000.

questions.q: A sum of ₦250,000 is invested at simple interest for 5 years, and the total interest earned is ₦62,500. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.e: Using I = PRT/100, 62500 = (250000 x R x 5)/100, so R = (62500 x 100)/(250000 x 5) = 5%. This gives the annual rate.
questions.p: Use di formula I = PRT/100. Put 62500 for interest, 250000 for principal, and 5 for time to solve and get R = 5%.

questions.q: A trader marks up the price of a bag of rice by 25% above the cost price of ₦40,000, then gives a discount of 8% on the marked price to a customer. Find the amount the customer pays.
questions.e: Marked price = 40000 x 1.25 = 50000. After 8% discount, amount paid = 50000 x 0.92 = 46000. This involves two successive percentage steps.
questions.p: Find di marked price by multiplying 40000 by 1.25 to get 50000. Then remove 8% discount to remain with 46000.

questions.q: A man wants to invest money at simple interest so that it doubles in 8 years. What annual rate of interest, in percent, must he use?
questions.e: For the money to double, interest earned equals the principal, so P = P x R x 8/100, giving R = 100/8 = 12.5%. This is a standard simple interest relation.
questions.p: Since money double, interest equal principal. Put am inside formula to get R = 100/8, which give 12.5%.

questions.q: The pressure P of a gas varies inversely as its volume V at constant temperature. If P = 20 units when V = 15 cm³, find P when V = 25 cm³.
questions.e: Since P varies inversely as V, PV is constant: 20 x 15 = 300. When V = 25, P = 300/25 = 12 units.
questions.p: Since P dey vary inversely as V, we know say PV na constant. If we multiply 20 by 15, we get 300. So, if V na 25, P go be 300 divide by 25, wey give us 12 units.

questions.q: In a certain company, the total allowance A paid to a staff is partly constant and partly varies as the number of years of service, N. A staff with 3 years of service receives ₦45,000, while a staff with 7 years of service receives ₦65,000. Find the constant part of the allowance.
questions.e: Let A = a + bN. From the two equations: 45000 = a + 3b and 65000 = a + 7b. Subtracting gives 4b = 20000, so b = 5000, and a = 45000 - 15000 = 30000.
questions.p: We use formula A = a + bN. When we solve the two equations, we find say b na 5000. If we put that one inside, we go get 45000 minus 15000, so the constant part na 30000.

questions.q: If y is directly proportional to x, and x is inversely proportional to the square of z, what is the relationship between y and z?

y varies directly as the square of z
questions.e: Since y = kx and x = m/z², substituting gives y = km/z², which means y varies inversely as the square of z.
questions.p: If y dey proportional to x, and x dey inversely proportional to z squared, we go just join dem together. This one mean say y go vary inversely as the square of z.

questions.q: The electrical resistance R of a wire varies directly as its length L and inversely as the square of its diameter D. A wire of length 8 m and diameter 2 mm has a resistance of 32 ohms. Find the resistance of a wire of the same material with length 12 m and diameter 3 mm.
questions.e: R = kL/D², so 32 = k(8)/4, giving k = 16. For the new wire, R = 16(12)/9 = 192/9 = 21.33 ohms.
questions.p: We use the formula R = kL/D squared to find k, wey be 16. When we put the new length and diameter inside, we get 16 times 12 divide by 9, wey give us 21.33 ohms.

questions.q: Musa's weekly transport cost T is partly constant and partly varies directly as the number of trips, n, he makes. When he makes 4 trips, his cost is ₦2400, and when he makes 10 trips, his cost is ₦4800. Find the cost when he makes 6 trips.
questions.e: Let T = a + bn. From the equations: 2400 = a + 4b and 4800 = a + 10b. Subtracting gives 6b = 2400, so b = 400, and a = 2400 - 1600 = 800. For n = 6, T = 800 + 2400 = 3200.
questions.p: We use T = a + bn to solve for a and b, wey give us 800 and 400. When we put 6 trips inside the formula, we get 800 plus 2400, so the total cost na 3200.

questions.q: The quantity Z varies directly as x and inversely as y. If Z = 12 when x = 6 and y = 2, find Z when x = 9 and y = 3.
questions.e: Z = k × x/y, so 12 = k × 6/2 gives k = 4. Then Z = 4 × 9/3 = 12.
questions.p: We write di variation as Z = k times x divide by y. When we put di first values, we get k = 4, and when we solve again for x = 9 and y = 3, Z go give us 12.

questions.q: In a school cooperative, the amount of interest I paid on a loan is partly constant and partly varies directly as the number of months n the loan is kept. A member who kept a loan for 2 months paid ₦2500, while another who kept it for 5 months paid ₦4000. Find the amount paid by a member who kept the loan for 8 months.
questions.e: Let I = a + bn. From the two equations: a + 2b = 2500 and a + 5b = 4000, so 3b = 1500, b = 500 and a = 1500. For n = 8, I = 1500 + 500(8) = 5500.
questions.p: Make we write di formula as I = a + bn and use di two information to find a = 1500 and b = 500. When we put n = 8 inside di equation, we go get ₦5500.

questions.q: If y is inversely proportional to x, which of the following graphs would give a straight line when plotted?
questions.e: Since y varies inversely as x, y = k/x, which means y is directly proportional to 1/x. Plotting y against 1/x gives a straight line through the origin.
questions.p: Since y dey inversely proportional to x, e mean say y = k divide by x. If you plot y against 1 divide by x, na im go give you straight line graph.

questions.q: A quantity Q varies directly as the square root of P. If P increases by 44%, find the percentage increase in Q.
questions.e: Q = k × √P. If P becomes 1.44P, √1.44 = 1.2, so Q increases by 20 percent.
questions.p: From Q = k root P, if P increase by 44 percent, e mean say e multiply by 1.44. When you find root of 1.44, you get 1.2, wey be 20 percent increase for Q.

questions.q: If a varies directly as b, and b varies inversely as the square of c, what is the relationship between a and c?
questions.e: Since a = kb and b = m/c², substituting gives a = km/c², so a varies inversely as the square of c.
questions.p: Since a dey equal to constant times b, and b dey equal to constant divide by c square, when you put them together, a go vary inversely as c square.

questions.q: Chidi is p years old and his sister is q years old. The sum of their ages is 35, and twice Chidi's age exceeds his sister's age by 10. Find Chidi's age, p.
questions.e: From p+q=35 and 2p-q=10, add both equations to get 3p=45, so p=15.
questions.p: If we add the two equations together, we go get 3p = 45. When you divide both sides by 3, you get p = 15.

questions.q: A plot of land in Enugu is sold for ₦x per square metre. Okafor bought a plot of 150 square metres and paid a total that was ₦45,000 more than what Eze paid for a 90 square metre plot at the same rate. Find the price per square metre, x.
questions.e: The equation is 150x - 90x = 45000, so 60x = 45000, giving x = 750.
questions.p: We go minus 90x from 150x to get 60x, wey equal 45000. If you divide 45000 by 60, x go give you 750.

questions.q: Solve the linear inequality: 3(x - 2) + 4 <= 2x + 5.
questions.e: Expanding gives 3x - 6 + 4 <= 2x + 5, so 3x - 2 <= 2x + 5, which simplifies to x <= 7.

questions.q: Solve the equation x² - 9x + 20 = 0.

questions.p: Total surface area of cube na 6(side)². When you solve 150 = 6s², side go be 5 cm, and volume na 5³ wey be 125 cm³.

questions.p: Volume of pyramid na one third times base area times height. E come be (1/3) × (10 × 10) × 12, wey give us 400 cm³.

questions.q: A rectangular field has length 36 m and width 15 m. Find the length of the diagonal of the field.
questions.e: By Pythagoras, diagonal = √(36² + 15²) = √(1296 + 225) = √1521 = 39 m.
questions.p: To find di diagonal, we use Pythagoras theorem. We square 36 and 15, add dem to get 1521, and take di square root to get 39 m.

questions.q: The parallel sides of a trapezium-shaped plot are 20 m and 32 m, and the plot has an area of 390 m². Find the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides.

questions.p: We use di area formula for trapezium, wey be 1/2 (a+b)h. When we put di values, 390 = 26 x h, so we divide 390 by 26 to get 15 m.

questions.q: A hollow metal pipe has an external diameter of 10 cm and an internal diameter of 8 cm. Find the cross-sectional area of the metal used. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.e: Cross-sectional area = π(R² - r²) where R = 5 cm and r = 4 cm, giving 22/7 x (25 - 16) = 22/7 x 9 = 198/7 = 28.29 cm².
questions.p: We use di area formula for hollow shape, π times R square minus r square. With R = 5 cm and r = 4 cm, we get 22/7 times 9, wey give us 28.29 cm².

questions.q: Find the equation of the line passing through the points (2, 5) and (4, 11).

questions.q: A line L has equation 2x + 5y = 20. Find the gradient of any line parallel to L.
questions.e: Rewriting 2x + 5y = 20 as y = -2/5 x + 4 shows the gradient is -2/5. A parallel line has the same gradient.
questions.p: If we rearrange 2x + 5y = 20 to look like y = -2/5 x + 4, we go see say the gradient na -2/5. Dem parallel lines must get the exact same gradient.

questions.q: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining P(2, 1) and Q(6, 5).
questions.e: Midpoint of PQ is (4,3) and gradient of PQ is (5-1)/(6-2)=1, so perpendicular gradient is -1. Using point (4,3): y - 3 = -1(x - 4) gives y = -x + 7.
questions.p: Midpoint of PQ na (4, 3) and gradient na 1, so the perpendicular gradient na -1. If we put am inside point-slope form with (4, 3), e go give us y = -x + 7.

questions.q: A triangle has vertices A(0, 0), B(4, 0), and C(4, 3). Find the angle which line AC makes with the positive x-axis, to the nearest degree.
questions.e: Gradient of AC = (3-0)/(4-0) = 3/4, so the angle = arctan(3/4) which is about 37 degrees. This is the base angle of the right triangle formed.
questions.p: Gradient of line AC na (3-0)/(4-0) wey be 3/4. When you find arctan(3/4), e go give you approximately 37 degrees.

questions.q: Three points X(1, 2), Y(4, k), and Z(7, 14) lie on a straight line. Find the value of k.
questions.e: Since the points are collinear, the gradient between X and Y equals the gradient between Y and Z. Using gradient XZ = (14-2)/(7-1) = 2, then k = 2 + 2(4-1) = 8.
questions.p: Because the points dey straight line, the gradient from X to Y must equal the gradient from X to Z. If we solve am, we go get k = 8.

questions.q: A line passes through the point (-2, 3) and has gradient -1/2. Find the equation of the line.
questions.e: Using y - 3 = -1/2(x - (-2)) gives y - 3 = -1/2 x - 1, so y = -1/2 x + 2, which rearranges to x + 2y = 4.
questions.p: Make you put point (-2, 3) and gradient -1/2 inside formula y - y1 = m(x - x1). E go give you y - 3 = -1/2(x + 2). When you expand and rearrange am, e go come be x + 2y = 4.

questions.q: Find the gradient of a line that is perpendicular to the line joining A(1, -2) and B(5, 6).
questions.e: Gradient of AB = (6-(-2))/(5-1) = 8/4 = 2. The perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal, which is -1/2.
questions.p: First, find gradient of line AB by doing change in y over change in x, wey be (6-(-2))/(5-1) to get 2. Because perpendicular gradient na negative reciprocal, you go turn am upside down and put minus to get -1/2.

questions.q: A triangle has vertices P(2, 3), Q(6, 3), and R(2, 8). Calculate the length of the hypotenuse QR of this right-angled triangle.
questions.e: QR connects (6,3) and (2,8), so its length is √((6-2)²+(3-8)²) = √(16+25) = √41. PQ and PR are the two shorter sides meeting at the right angle at P.
questions.p: Use distance formula between points Q(6,3) and R(2,8). E go give you square root of (6-2)² plus (3-8)², wey be square root of 16 + 25. Na so you go get √41.

questions.q: The line 3x - 2y + 6 = 0 crosses the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. Find the distance AB.
questions.e: Setting y=0 gives x=-2, so A(-2,0). Setting x=0 gives y=3, so B(0,3). Distance AB = √((0-(-2))²+(3-0)²) = √(4+9) = √13.
questions.p: Put y=0 to find where line touch x-axis at A(-2,0), and put x=0 to find where e touch y-axis at B(0,3). Use distance formula between A and B, you go get square root of (2² + 3²), wey be √13.

questions.q: A line has x-intercept 4 and y-intercept -6. Find the equation of this line in the form ax + by + c = 0.
questions.e: The line passes through (4,0) and (0,-6), giving gradient (−6−0)/(0−4) = 3/2. Using y - 0 = 3/2(x - 4) leads to 2y = 3x - 12, which rearranges to 3x - 2y - 12 = 0.
questions.p: The points na (4,0) and (0,-6), so gradient na 3/2. If you use intercept form or point-slope form, e go give you 2y = 3x - 12. Rearrange am well, e go come be 3x - 2y - 12 = 0.

questions.q: A surveyor at point X observes a tower at an angle of elevation of 30°. He walks 40 m closer to the tower, to point Y, and observes the angle of elevation as 60°. Find the height of the tower (in metres), leaving your answer as a surd where necessary.
questions.e: Let height = h. From X, distance = h/tan30 = h × √3; from Y, distance = h/tan60 = h/√3. The difference in distances is 40, so h × √3 - h/√3 = 40, giving h × (2/√3) = 40, so h = 20 √3.
questions.p: Make we call the height h. If you use tan 30 and tan 60, you go see say h times (2/√3) equal to 40. When you solve am, you go get h equal to 20 √3.

questions.q: Find the value of cos 150° without using a calculator.

questions.p: 150 degree dey for second quadrant where cosine dey negative. Because 150 degree na 180 minus 30, the answer na minus cos 30 which be -√3/2.

questions.q: Two ships leave a port at the same time. Ship A sails on a bearing of 030° at 20 km/h, and ship B sails on a bearing of 120° at 15 km/h. After 2 hours, how far apart are the two ships, correct to the nearest kilometre?
questions.e: After 2 hours, ship A is 40 km from port and ship B is 30 km from port. The angle between bearings 030° and 120° is 90°, so by Pythagoras, the distance apart is √(40² + 30²) = √2500 = 50 km.
questions.p: After two hours, ship A don travel 40 km and ship B don travel 30 km. Because the angle between dem na 90 degree, you go use Pythagoras theorem to get √(40² + 30²) wey be 50 km.

questions.q: If sin theta = 3/5 and theta is obtuse (90° < theta < 180°), find the value of cos theta.
questions.e: Using sin² theta + cos² theta = 1, cos theta = ±4/5. Since theta is obtuse, cosine is negative in the second quadrant, so cos theta = -4/5.
questions.p: If sin theta na 3/5, then cos theta go be 4/5. Because theta dey obtuse, cosine must be negative, so the answer na -4/5.

questions.q: Simplify: sin 60° cos 30° + cos 60° sin 30°, giving your answer without using a calculator.
questions.e: This expression is the expansion of sin(60° + 30°) = sin 90° = 1, using the sine addition formula sin A cos B + cos A sin B = sin(A+B).

questions.q: Find dy/dx if y = (2x + 1)/(x - 3), where x is not equal to 3.
questions.e: Using the quotient rule, dy/dx = [2(x-3) - (2x+1)(1)]/(x-3)² = (2x-6-2x-1)/(x-3)² = -7/(x-3)².
questions.p: We use quotient rule for this differentiation. When we differentiate (2x + 1)/(x - 3), we get -7/(x-3)².

questions.q: A small business owner, Ngozi, finds that her weekly profit in naira is P(x) = -2x² + 240x - 1000, where x is the number of bags of rice sold. Find the number of bags that must be sold to maximize her profit.
questions.e: dP/dx = -4x + 240 = 0 gives x = 60. This is the value of x that maximizes the profit since the coefficient of x² is negative.
questions.p: To find the maximum profit, we differentiate P(x) and set am to zero. When we solve -4x + 240 = 0, we get x = 60.

questions.q: The volume of a cube is increasing at a rate of 12 cm³/s. Find the rate at which the side length is increasing when the side length is 2 cm.
questions.e: V = x³ so dV/dt = 3x² (dx/dt). At x=2, 12 = 3(4)(dx/dt), giving dx/dt = 1 cm/s.
questions.p: We use chain rule for V = x³, so dV/dt = 3x²(dx/dt). If we put 12 for dV/dt and 2 for x, we go get dx/dt = 1 cm/s.

questions.q: Find the second derivative of y = 5x⁴ - 2x³ + x with respect to x.
questions.e: The first derivative is 20x³ - 6x² + 1, and differentiating again gives 60x² - 12x.
questions.p: First, we differentiate 5x⁴ - 2x³ + x to get 20x³ - 6x² + 1. When we differentiate am again, we get 60x² - 12x.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward so that its height in metres after t seconds is h(t) = 30t - 5t². Find the maximum height reached by the stone.

questions.p: We differentiate h(t) and set am to zero to find the time t = 3 seconds. When we put t = 3 inside the original equation, we get 45 m as the maximum height.

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the point on the curve y = x² - 6x + 11 where the gradient is zero.

questions.p: Gradient na zero mean say dy/dx = 0. If we solve 2x - 6 = 0, we get x = 3, and when we put x = 3 inside the curve equation, y = 2.

questions.q: Find the values of x for which the curve y = 2x³ - 3x² - 12x + 5 is decreasing.

questions.q: Find ∫ (√x + 1/√x) dx
questions.e: Write √x as x^(1/2) and 1/√x as x^(-1/2). Integrating gives (2/3)x^(3/2) and 2x^(1/2) respectively, so the sum is (2/3)x^(3/2) + 2x^(1/2) + C.

questions.q: Find the area bounded by the curve y = 9 - x², the x-axis, from x = -3 to x = 3.

questions.q: A manufacturing company in Aba finds that its marginal cost function is MC = 3x² + 4x + 10, where x is the number of units produced. Find the total cost function C(x), given that the fixed cost (cost when x = 0) is ₦500.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed between the curves y = x² and y = 2x, for x between 0 and 2.

questions.q: A trader's cost function for producing x bags of garri is given by C(x) = ∫(2x + 30) dx. If the fixed cost (cost when x = 0) is ₦500, find the total cost of producing 10 bags.
questions.e: Integrating gives C(x) = x² + 30x + C. Since C(0) = 500, the constant C equals 500, so C(x) = x² + 30x + 500. At x = 10, C(10) = 100 + 300 + 500 = 900.
questions.p: When you integrate 2x + 30, you go get x² + 30x + C. Since the fixed cost na 500, the equation be x² + 30x + 500, so for 10 bags, you go get 100 + 300 + 500 = 900.

questions.q: Find the area between the curve y = x² - 4 and the x-axis, bounded between x = -2 and x = 2.

questions.p: Because the curve dey below the x-axis, you must take the absolute value of the integral. The integral of x² - 4 from -2 to 2 give -32/3, so the area na 32/3.

questions.q: In how many ways can 3 Mathematics books and 2 Physics books be arranged on a shelf so that the 2 Physics books are always kept next to each other?
questions.e: Treat the 2 Physics books as one single block, giving 4 items in total to arrange, which can be done in 4! = 24 ways. The 2 Physics books within the block can be arranged in 2! = 2 ways, giving 24 x 2 = 48.
questions.p: Make we join the 2 Physics books together as one block, come arrange the 4 items as 4! = 24. Since the two Physics books fit rearrange themselves in 2! = 2 ways, 24 times 2 give us 48.

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.e: There are 2³ = 8 equally likely outcomes. The outcomes with exactly 2 heads are HHT, HTH, THH, which are 3 outcomes. So the probability is 3/8.
questions.p: Total outcome na 2 raised to power 3 wey be 8. The ones wey get exactly 2 heads na 3, so di probability na 3/8.

questions.q: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled standard deck of 52 playing cards. What is the probability that the card is a king or a queen?
questions.e: There are 4 kings and 4 queens, giving 8 favourable cards out of 52. This simplifies to 8/52 = 2/13.
questions.p: We get 4 kings and 4 queens, so join join dem together na 8 favourable cards out of 52. When you reduce 8/52, e go give you 2/13.

questions.q: Two events A and B are such that P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and A and B are independent events. Find P(A and B).
questions.e: For independent events, P(A and B) equals P(A) multiplied by P(B). So P(A and B) = 0.4 x 0.5 = 0.2.
questions.p: For independent events, just multiply P(A) and P(B) together. Na 0.4 multiply by 0.5 wey give us 0.2.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled and a fair coin is tossed at the same time. What is the probability of obtaining a number greater than 4 on the die and a head on the coin?
questions.e: The probability of a number greater than 4 (that is, 5 or 6) on the die is 2/6 = 1/3, and the probability of a head is 1/2. Since the two events are independent, multiply them: 1/3 x 1/2 = 1/6.
questions.p: Probability of number greater than 4 for die na 2/6 which be 1/3, and for head na 1/2. Just multiply 1/3 and 1/2 together to get 1/6.

questions.q: A box contains 6 identical balls numbered 1 to 6. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both balls drawn have even numbers?
questions.e: There are 3 even numbered balls (2, 4, 6) out of 6. The probability the first ball is even is 3/6, and given that, the probability the second is also even is 2/5. Multiplying gives (3/6) x (2/5) = 1/5.
questions.p: Even numbers inside di box na 3, so first one na 3/6. Since dem no replace am, di second one na 2/5, and when you multiply dem, e go give you 1/5.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of obtaining a number greater than 4?
questions.e: The numbers greater than 4 on a die are 5 and 6, giving 2 favourable outcomes out of 6. So the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.
questions.p: Na 5 and 6 be di numbers wey dey greater than 4 for die, e give us 2 out of 6. When you reduce am, e come be 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.q: Musa has two bags. Bag A contains 3 red beads and 2 black beads. Bag B contains 4 red beads and 1 black bead. If he picks one bead at random from each bag, what is the probability that both beads are red?
questions.e: The probability of red from Bag A is 3/5 and from Bag B is 4/5. Since the picks are independent, multiply: (3/5) x (4/5) = 12/25.
questions.p: Probability say red go come out for Bag A na 3/5, and for Bag B na 4/5. Since dem dey independent, just multiply dem: (3/5) x (4/5) = 12/25.

questions.q: A box contains 5 good phone chargers and 3 faulty ones, all looking alike. Two chargers are picked one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both chargers picked are faulty?
questions.e: The probability the first is faulty is 3/8. Without replacement, the probability the second is also faulty is 2/7. Multiplying gives (3/8) x (2/7) = 6/56 = 3/28.
questions.p: Probability for first faulty charger na 3/8, and since dem no return am, di second one na 2/7. Multiply dem together to get (3/8) x (2/7) = 3/28.

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, 18 study Physics, 15 study Chemistry, and 7 study both Physics and Chemistry. If a student is picked at random from the class, what is the probability that the student studies Physics or Chemistry?
questions.e: Using the addition rule, P(Physics or Chemistry) = P(Physics) + P(Chemistry) - P(both) = 18/40 + 15/40 - 7/40 = 26/40. This accounts for students counted twice in both subjects.
questions.p: We go use addition rule, add Physics and Chemistry, then minus di ones wey do both. E go give us 18/40 + 15/40 - 7/40 = 26/40.

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed and a fair die is rolled together. What is the probability of getting a tail on the coin and an even number on the die?
questions.e: The probability of a tail is 1/2 and the probability of an even number (2, 4, or 6) is 3/6 = 1/2. Since the events are independent, multiply: (1/2) x (1/2) = 1/4.
questions.p: Probability for tail na 1/2, while even number for die na 3/6 which be 1/2. Multiply di two independent probabilities to get (1/2) x (1/2) = 1/4.

questions.q: A hawker at Onitsha market has 20 oranges, of which 4 are bad. If 3 oranges are selected at random without replacement, what is the probability that all 3 selected oranges are good?
questions.e: There are 16 good oranges out of 20. The probability all three picked are good is (16/20) x (15/19) x (14/18) = 3360/6840 = 560/1140, when simplified using successive conditional probabilities without replacement.
questions.p: We get 16 good oranges out of 20, and we dey pick dem one after di other without replacement. As we multiply di probabilities, e go give us 560/1140.

questions.q: Two events P and Q are such that P(P) = 0.3, P(Q) = 0.25, and P(P and Q) = 0.1. Find P(P or Q).
questions.e: Using the addition rule for probability, P(P or Q) = P(P) + P(Q) - P(P and Q) = 0.3 + 0.25 - 0.1 = 0.45. This avoids double counting the overlap.
questions.p: To find P(P or Q), we go add P(P) and P(Q) then minus di intersection. E go give us 0.3 + 0.25 - 0.1 = 0.45.

questions.q: A bag contains 8 balls numbered 1 to 8. A ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that the number on the ball is a multiple of 3 or a multiple of 4?
questions.e: Multiples of 3 up to 8 are 3 and 6 (2 numbers), while multiples of 4 are 4 and 8 (2 numbers), with no overlap. So the total favourable outcomes are 4 out of 8, giving 4/8 = 1/2.
questions.p: Multiples of 3 na 3 and 6, while multiples of 4 na 4 and 8, wey make dem 4 favourable numbers in total. So di probability na 4/8 = 1/2.
